translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 101.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 101.

sentences.zh: 【晉紀二十三】起上章涒灘，盡著雍執徐，凡九年。

translations.literal: [Jin Annals 23] From Shangzhang Tuntan through Zhuoyong Zhixu; nine years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Jin Annals 23] From Shangzhang Tuntan through Zhuoyong Zhixu—nine years in all.

sentences.zh: 孝宗穆皇帝下升平四年（

translations.literal: The fourth year of Shengping under Emperor Xiaozong Mu (
translations.idiomatic: Fourth year of Shengping, reign of Emperor Xiaozong Mu (

sentences.zh: 庚申，公元三六零年）

translations.literal: gengshen, AD 360)
translations.idiomatic: gengshen year, AD 360)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，癸巳，燕主俊大閱於鄴，欲使大司馬恪、司空陽騖將之入寇；

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on guisi day, the Yan ruler Jun held a grand review at Ye, intending to have the Grand Marshal Ke and the Minister of Works Yang Chi lead them in an invasion;
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on guisi day, the Yan ruler Murong Jun held a grand military review at Ye. He planned to have Grand Marshal Murong Ke and Minister of Works Yang Chi lead a raid into Jin territory;

sentences.zh: 會疾篤，乃召恪、騖及司徒評、領軍將軍慕輿根等受遺詔輔政。

translations.literal: but he fell gravely ill, and so summoned Ke, Chi, and the Minister over the Masses Ping, the Palace Guard general Murong Gen, and others to receive his deathbed edict and assist in government.
translations.idiomatic: He then fell seriously ill and summoned Murong Ke, Yang Chi, Minister over the Masses Murong Ping, Palace Guard general Murong Gen, and others to receive his deathbed edict and serve as regents.

sentences.zh: 甲午，卒。

translations.literal: On jiawu day he died.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu day he died.

sentences.zh: 戊子，太子暐即位，年十一。

translations.literal: On wuzi day the crown prince Wei acceded to the throne; he was eleven years old.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi day Crown Prince Murong Wei took the throne at the age of eleven.

sentences.zh: 大赦，改元建熙。

translations.literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed, and the era name was changed to Jianxi.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Jianxi.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅分司、隸置雍州，以河南公雙為都督雍、河、涼三州諸軍事、征西大將軍、雍州刺史，改封趙公，鎮安定。

translations.literal: The Qin king Jian divided Sili and established Yong Province, appointing Duke of Henan Shuang as overseer of military affairs for Yong, He, and Liang provinces, Grand General Who Conquers the West, and governor of Yong; he was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao and stationed at Anding.
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian of Former Qin carved Yong Province out of the metropolitan region and appointed Duke of Henan Fu Shuang commander-in-chief for Yong, He, and Liang, Grand General Who Conquers the West, and governor of Yong. Shuang was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao and posted at Anding.

sentences.zh: 封弟忠為河南公。

translations.literal: His younger brother Zhong was enfeoffed as Duke of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Fu Zhong was enfeoffed as Duke of Henan.

sentences.zh: 仇池公楊俊卒，子世立。

translations.literal: The Duke of Chouchi, Yang Jun, died; his son Shi succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jun, Duke of Chouchi, died, and his son Yang Shi succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 二月，燕人尊可足渾後為皇太后。

translations.literal: In the second month the people of Yan honored Empress Kezu Hun as empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the Yan court honored Empress Kezu Hun as empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 以太原王恪為太宰，專錄朝政；

translations.literal: The Prince of Taiyuan, Ke, was made Grand Preceptor with sole charge of recording court affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ke, Prince of Taiyuan, was appointed Grand Preceptor with sole authority over the daily record of government;

sentences.zh: 上庸王評為太傅，陽騖為太保，慕輿根為太師，參輔朝政。

translations.literal: the Prince of Shangyong, Ping, was made Grand Tutor; Yang Chi was made Grand Guardian; Murong Gen was made Grand Master; and they jointly assisted in government.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ping, Prince of Shangyong, became Grand Tutor; Yang Chi became Grand Guardian; Murong Gen became Grand Master; and all three shared in assisting the government.

sentences.zh: 根性木強，自恃先朝勳舊，心不服恪，舉動倨傲。

translations.literal: Gen was stubborn by nature; relying on his merit from the previous reign, he did not submit to Ke in his heart and behaved with arrogant insolence.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Gen was stiff and unyielding by nature. Counting on his service under the late emperor, he refused in his heart to defer to Murong Ke and carried himself with arrogant insolence.

sentences.zh: 時太后可足渾氏頗預外事，根欲為亂，乃言於恪曰：「今主上幼沖，母后干政，殿下宜防意外之變，思有以自全。

translations.literal: At that time the empress dowager Kezu Hun was much involved in external affairs. Gen wished to stir up trouble and therefore said to Ke: "The sovereign is young and the empress dowager meddles in government. Your Highness ought to guard against unforeseen changes and think how to preserve yourself.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager Kezu Hun was then deeply involved in state affairs. Murong Gen, scheming to raise trouble, said to Murong Ke: "The emperor is still a child and the empress dowager interferes in government. Your Highness should guard against unforeseen upheavals and find a way to secure yourself.

sentences.zh: 且定天下者，殿下之功也。

translations.literal: Moreover, it was Your Highness's achievement that settled the realm.
translations.idiomatic: It was your achievement, moreover, that pacified the realm.

sentences.zh: 兄亡弟及，古今成法，俟畢山陵，宜廢主上為王，殿下自踐尊位，以為大燕無窮之福。

translations.literal: When an elder brother dies a younger brother succeeds—this is the established law of past and present. After the imperial tomb rites are completed, you should depose the sovereign and make him a prince, while Your Highness yourself ascends the supreme position, thereby securing boundless blessing for Great Yan."
translations.idiomatic: When an elder brother dies, a younger brother succeeds—the law of every age. Once the imperial burial is finished, you should depose the emperor and make him a prince, while you yourself take the throne. That would be boundless fortune for Great Yan."

sentences.zh: 」恪曰：「公醉邪？

translations.literal: " Ke said: "Are you drunk, sir?
translations.idiomatic: " Murong Ke said, "Are you drunk, sir?

sentences.zh: 何言之悖也！

translations.literal: How perverse are your words!
translations.idiomatic: How perverse your words are!

sentences.zh: 吾與公受先帝遺詔，云何而遽有此議？

translations.literal: You and I received the late emperor's deathbed edict—how can you suddenly advance such a proposal?
translations.idiomatic: You and I received the late emperor's deathbed edict—how can you suddenly propose such a thing?

sentences.zh: 」根愧謝而退。

translations.literal: " Gen withdrew in shame and apology.
translations.idiomatic: " Murong Gen withdrew, ashamed and apologizing.

sentences.zh: 恪以告吳王垂，垂勸恪誅之。

translations.literal: Ke reported this to the Prince of Wu, Chui, who urged Ke to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ke told Murong Chui, Prince of Wu, who urged that Murong Gen be put to death.

sentences.zh: 恪曰：「今新遭大喪，二鄰觀釁，而宰輔自相誅夷，恐乖遠近之望，且可忍之。

translations.literal: Ke said: "We have just suffered a great bereavement, and our two neighbors watch for openings. If the chief ministers slaughter one another, I fear we will disappoint expectations near and far; for the time being we must bear with him."
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ke said, "We have only just lost the emperor, and our two neighbors are watching for weakness. If the chief ministers begin killing one another, we will disappoint everyone near and far. For now we must endure him."

sentences.zh: 」秘書臨皇甫真言於恪曰：「根本庸豎，過蒙先帝厚恩，引參顧命。

translations.literal: " The Secretariat attendant Huangfu Zhen said to Ke: "Gen is a vulgar fellow who received excessive favor from the late emperor and was brought in to share the regency.
translations.idiomatic: " Huangfu Zhen of the Secretariat said to Murong Ke, "Murong Gen is a coarse nobody who received far too much favor from the late emperor and was admitted to the regency.

sentences.zh: 而小人無識，自國哀已來，驕很日甚，將成禍亂。

translations.literal: Yet this petty man lacks understanding; since the national mourning began his arrogance and harshness grow daily, and he will bring about disaster and rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the man is ignorant and base. Since the mourning began his arrogance and violence have grown daily, and he will soon bring ruin upon the state.

sentences.zh: 明公今日居周公之地，當為社稷深謀，早為之所。

translations.literal: Your Excellency today stands in the place of the Duke of Zhou; you ought to plan deeply for the altars of state and deal with this early."
translations.idiomatic: You stand today where the Duke of Zhou stood. You must plan deeply for the altars of state and act before it is too late."

sentences.zh: 」恪不聽。

translations.literal: " Ke would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: " Murong Ke would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 根又言於可足渾氏及燕主暐曰：「太宰、太傅將謀不軌，臣請帥禁兵以誅之。

translations.literal: Gen again spoke to Kezu Hun and the Yan ruler Wei: "The Grand Preceptor and Grand Tutor are plotting treason; I request to lead the palace guard to execute them."
translations.idiomatic: Murong Gen then spoke to Kezu Hun and Emperor Murong Wei: "The Grand Preceptor and Grand Tutor are plotting treason. I ask leave to lead the palace guard and put them to death."

sentences.zh: 」可足渾氏將從之，暐曰：「二公，國之親賢，先帝選之，托以孤嫠，必不肯爾。

translations.literal: " Kezu Hun was about to agree. Wei said: "These two lords are the state's close and worthy men; the late emperor chose them and entrusted the orphan and widow to them—they surely would not act thus.
translations.idiomatic: " Kezu Hun was about to consent. Murong Wei said, "Those two men are the state's closest and worthiest ministers. The late emperor chose them and entrusted the orphan and the widow to them. They would never do such a thing.

sentences.zh: 安知非太師欲為亂也！

translations.literal: Who knows whether it is not the Grand Master who wishes to make trouble!
translations.idiomatic: Who knows whether it is not the Grand Master who means to raise trouble!

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: " And so the matter was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " The plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 根又思戀東土，言於可足渾氏及暐曰：「今天下蕭條，外寇非一，國大憂深，不如還東。

translations.literal: Gen again longed for the eastern homeland and said to Kezu Hun and Wei: "The realm today is desolate; foreign enemies are not one alone; the state's great troubles run deep—it would be better to return east."
translations.idiomatic: Murong Gen, homesick for the eastern lands, told Kezu Hun and Murong Wei, "The realm is desolate, foreign enemies press on every side, and the state's troubles run deep. We would do better to return east."

sentences.zh: 」恪聞之，乃與太傅評謀，密奏根罪狀，使右衛將軍傅顏就內省誅根，並其妻子、黨與。

translations.literal: " When Ke heard of this, he plotted with the Grand Tutor Ping, secretly memorialized Gen's crimes, and had the Right Guard general Fu Yan enter the inner palace to execute Gen, together with his wife, children, and partisans.
translations.idiomatic: " When Murong Ke learned of this, he plotted with Grand Tutor Murong Ping, secretly memorialized Murong Gen's crimes, and sent Right Guard general Fu Yan into the inner palace to execute Gen along with his wife, children, and followers.

sentences.zh: 大赦。

translations.literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 是時新遭大喪，誅夷狼籍，內外恟懼，太宰恪舉止如常，人不見其有憂色，每出入，一人步從。

translations.literal: At this time the court had just suffered a great bereavement; executions lay strewn about; inside and outside all were alarmed and afraid. Grand Preceptor Ke conducted himself as usual; people did not see worry on his face. Each time he went out or in, only one man followed on foot.
translations.idiomatic: The court had only just buried its emperor, and executions lay scattered everywhere. Inside and outside the palace people were terrified. Yet Grand Preceptor Murong Ke carried himself as always; no one saw worry on his face, and whenever he went out or came in only a single attendant walked behind him.

sentences.zh: 或說以宜自戒備，恪曰：「人情方懼，當安重以鎮之，奈何復自驚擾，眾將何仰！

translations.literal: Some urged that he ought to take precautions for himself. Ke said: "Men's hearts are just now afraid; one should settle them with calm weight. How can we further alarm and disturb them—what will the multitude look up to!
translations.idiomatic: Some urged him to take precautions. Murong Ke said, "Men's hearts are already afraid. I must steady them with calm authority. How can I add to the panic? What would they have to rely on then?

sentences.zh: 」由是人心稍定。

translations.literal: " From this people's hearts gradually settled.
translations.idiomatic: " From that point minds began to steady.

sentences.zh: 恪雖綜大任，而朝廷之禮，兢兢嚴謹，每事必與司徒評議之，未嘗專決。

translations.literal: Although Ke held comprehensive great responsibility, in court ritual he was cautious and strict; in every matter he had to deliberate with Minister over the Masses Ping and never decided alone.
translations.idiomatic: Though Murong Ke held supreme authority, he observed court ritual with scrupulous care. On every matter he consulted Minister over the Masses Murong Ping and never decided alone.

sentences.zh: 虛心待士，咨詢善道，量才授任，人不逾位。

translations.literal: He received scholars with an open mind, sought counsel on the right Way, assigned office according to talent, and no man exceeded his proper place.
translations.idiomatic: He received scholars with an open mind, sought their counsel on good government, and assigned office according to talent so that no man held a post above his measure.

sentences.zh: 官屬、朝臣或有過失，不顯其狀，隨宜他敘，不令失倫，唯以此為貶。

translations.literal: If subordinates or court ministers had faults, he did not expose their circumstances but reassigned them elsewhere as appropriate, not letting them lose their proper rank—he used only this as demotion.
translations.idiomatic: When subordinates or court ministers erred, he did not expose their failings but transferred them to other posts suited to their abilities, never stripping them of proper rank. That alone was his form of demotion.

sentences.zh: 時人以為大愧，莫敢犯者。

translations.literal: Men of the time considered this a great shame, and none dared offend.
translations.idiomatic: Officials regarded this as a profound humiliation, and none dared give cause for it.

sentences.zh: 或有小過，自相責曰：「爾復欲望宰公遷官邪！

translations.literal: If someone had a small fault, he would blame himself, saying: "Do you again hope the chief minister will promote your office!
translations.idiomatic: When someone slipped even slightly, he would reproach himself: "Do you still expect the chief minister to advance you?

sentences.zh: 」朝廷初聞燕主俊卒，皆以為中原可圖。

translations.literal: " When the court first heard that the Yan ruler Jun had died, all thought the Central Plains could be taken.
translations.idiomatic: " When the Jin court first heard that Murong Jun of Yan had died, everyone thought the Central Plains could be recovered.

sentences.zh: 桓溫曰：「慕容恪尚在，憂方大耳。

translations.literal: Huan Wen said: "Murong Ke is still alive—the worry is only beginning."
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen said, "Murong Ke is still alive. Our troubles have only begun."

sentences.zh: 三月，己卯，葬燕主俊於龍陵，謚曰景昭皇帝，廟號烈祖。

translations.literal: In the third month, on jimao day, the Yan ruler Jun was buried at Longling; his posthumous title was Emperor Jingzhao, temple name Liezu.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on jimao day, Murong Jun of Yan was buried at Longling. His posthumous title was Emperor Jingzhao and his temple name Liezu.

sentences.zh: 所征郡國兵，以燕朝多難，互相驚動，往往擅自散歸，自鄴以南，道路斷塞。

translations.literal: The troops levied from commanderies and kingdoms, because the Yan court faced many troubles, alarmed one another and often dispersed and returned on their own; from Ye southward the roads were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: The troops levied from the commanderies and kingdoms, alarmed by Yan's many troubles, often dispersed and went home on their own. From Ye southward the roads were cut off.

sentences.zh: 太宰恪以吳王垂為使持節、征南將軍、都督河南諸軍事、兗州牧、荊州刺史，鎮梁國之蠡台，孫希為并州刺史，傅顏為護軍將軍，帥騎二萬，觀兵河南，臨淮而還，境內乃安。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor Ke appointed the Prince of Wu, Chui, as bearer of the staff of authority, General Who Conquers the South, overseer of military affairs for Henan, governor of Yan Province and inspector of Jing, stationed at Lixiang in Liang; Sun Xi as inspector of Bing; Fu Yan as Protector of the Army; and led twenty thousand cavalry to display forces in Henan, reaching the Huai and returning, after which the realm within the borders was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Murong Ke appointed Murong Chui, Prince of Wu, bearer of the staff of authority, General Who Conquers the South, commander for Henan, governor of Yan and inspector of Jing, with his seat at Lixiang in Liang. Sun Xi became inspector of Bing; Fu Yan became Protector of the Army. Murong Ke led twenty thousand cavalry to show force in Henan, marched to the Huai, and returned; only then did the realm within the borders grow calm.

sentences.zh: 希，泳之弟也。

translations.literal: Xi was the younger brother of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xi was the younger brother of Sun Yong.

sentences.zh: 匈奴劉衛辰遣使降秦，請田內地，春來秋返；

translations.literal: The Xiongnu Liu Weichen sent envoys to submit to Qin, requesting land to farm within the borders, coming in spring and returning in autumn;
translations.idiomatic: The Xiongnu leader Liu Weichen sent envoys to submit to Former Qin, asking for farmland inside the borders where his people might sow in spring and withdraw in autumn;

sentences.zh: 秦王堅許之。

translations.literal: the Qin king Jian granted it.
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian granted the request.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，雲中護軍賈雍遣司馬徐贇帥騎襲之，大獲而還。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Jia Yong, Protector of Yunzhong, sent the Major Xu Yun leading cavalry to raid him, gaining a great haul and returning.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Jia Yong, Protector of Yunzhong, sent his Major Xu Yun at the head of cavalry to raid him. They took a great haul and returned.

sentences.zh: 堅怒曰：「朕方以恩信懷戎狄，而汝貪小利以敗之，何也！

translations.literal: Jian angrily said: "I am just now winning over the barbarians with kindness and trust, yet you, greedy for small profit, have ruined it—why!
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian said in anger, "I am trying to win the tribes with kindness and good faith, and you have ruined it for a little plunder. Why?

sentences.zh: 」黜雍以白衣領職，遣使還其所獲，慰撫之。

translations.literal: " He demoted Yong to serve in plain dress while retaining his post, sent envoys to return what had been taken, and comforted Weichen.
translations.idiomatic: " He demoted Jia Yong to serve in plain dress while keeping his post, sent envoys to return everything taken, and reassured Liu Weichen.

sentences.zh: 衛辰於是居入塞內，貢獻相尋。

translations.literal: Weichen thereupon settled within the passes and sent tribute in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Weichen then settled inside the passes and sent tribute without interruption.

sentences.zh: 夏，六月，代王代翼犍妃慕容氏卒。

translations.literal: In summer, the sixth month, the Dai king's consort Murong, née Dai Yijian, died.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the sixth month, Murong, consort of the Dai king Tuoba Yijian, died.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，劉衛辰如代會葬，因求婚，什翼犍以女妻之。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Liu Weichen went to Dai to attend the funeral and, taking the occasion, sought a marriage alliance; Shiyijian gave him a daughter as wife.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Liu Weichen went to Dai for the funeral and asked for a marriage alliance. Tuoba Shiyijian gave him a daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 八月，辛丑朔，日有食之，既。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on xinchou, the first day of the month, there was a solar eclipse; it was total.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the first day xinchou, there was a total solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 謝安少有重名，前後徵辟，皆不就，寓居會稽，以山水、文籍自娛。

translations.literal: Xie An from youth had a great reputation; successive summonses to office he did not accept, residing in Kuaiji and amusing himself with mountains, waters, and books.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An had been famous from youth. Repeated summonses to office he declined, living in Kuaiji and devoting himself to landscape, literature, and quiet pleasure.

sentences.zh: 雖為布衣，時人皆以公輔期之，士大夫至相謂曰：「安石不出，當如蒼生何！

translations.literal: Although he was a commoner, men of the time all expected him to reach the highest offices; gentlemen even said to one another: "If Anshi does not come forth, what will become of the people!
translations.idiomatic: Though he remained a private gentleman, everyone expected him to reach the highest office. Scholars said to one another, "If Anshi will not come forth, what is to become of the people?

sentences.zh: 」安海游東山，常以妓女自隨。

translations.literal: " An wandered the eastern hills by the sea and often took singing girls with him.
translations.idiomatic: " Xie An roamed the eastern hills by the sea and often took musicians and courtesans with him.

sentences.zh: 司徒昱聞之，曰：「安石既與人同樂，必不得不與人同憂，召之必至。

translations.literal: Minister over the Masses Yu heard of it and said: "Anshi shares others' pleasures; he cannot fail to share others' sorrows as well—summon him and he is sure to come."
translations.idiomatic: Minister over the Masses Sima Yu heard of it and said, "Anshi knows how to share others' pleasures. He cannot fail to share their troubles as well. Summon him and he will come."

sentences.zh: 」安妻。

translations.literal: " An's wife
translations.idiomatic: " Xie An's wife

sentences.zh: 劉惔之妹也，見家門貴盛而安獨靜退，謂曰：「丈夫不如此也？

translations.literal: was the younger sister of Liu Tan. Seeing her clan's glory and splendor while An alone remained quiet and withdrawn, she said to him: "Is this how a man should be?
translations.idiomatic: was the younger sister of Liu Tan. Seeing her own clan's glory while her husband alone held back, she said to him, "Is this how a man should live?

sentences.zh: 」安掩鼻曰：「恐不免耳。

translations.literal: " An covered his nose and said: "I fear it cannot be avoided."
translations.idiomatic: " Xie An covered his nose and said, "I fear it cannot be avoided."

sentences.zh: 」及弟萬廢黜，安始有仕進之志，時已年四十餘。

translations.literal: " When his younger brother Wan was dismissed and disgraced, An first formed the will to advance in office; he was already past forty.
translations.idiomatic: " After his younger brother Xie Wan was dismissed in disgrace, Xie An first formed the wish to enter public life. He was already past forty.

sentences.zh: 征西大將軍桓溫請為司馬，安乃赴召，溫大喜，深禮重之。

translations.literal: Grand General Who Conquers the West Huan Wen requested him as Major; An then answered the summons. Wen was greatly pleased and treated him with deep courtesy and weight.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Who Conquers the West Huan Wen invited him to serve as his Major. Xie An answered the summons. Huan Wen was delighted and honored him with exceptional courtesy.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，烏桓獨孤部、鮮卑沒弈干各帥眾數萬降秦，秦王堅處之塞南。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, the Wuhuan of the Dugu tribe and the Xianbei Mobenqian each led tens of thousands in submission to Qin; the Qin king Jian settled them south of the passes.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, the Wuhuan Dugu tribe and the Xianbei Mobenqian each led tens of thousands to submit to Former Qin. King Fu Jian settled them south of the frontier passes.

sentences.zh: 陽平公融諫曰：「戎狄人面獸心，不知仁義。

translations.literal: Duke of Yangping Rong remonstrated, saying: "The barbarians have human faces but beast hearts and do not know benevolence and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Rong, Duke of Yangping, remonstrated: "These tribes have human faces but beast hearts. They know nothing of benevolence and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 其稽顙內附，實貪地利，非懷德也；

translations.literal: Their bowing and submission within the borders is in truth greed for the land's advantage, not cherishing virtue;
translations.idiomatic: Their bowing submission is really greed for good land, not gratitude for kindness;

sentences.zh: 不敢犯邊；

translations.literal: their not daring to violate the frontier
translations.idiomatic: their not daring to raid the frontier

sentences.zh: 實憚兵威，非感恩也。

translations.literal: is in truth fear of military might, not gratitude for kindness.
translations.idiomatic: is really fear of our arms, not thankfulness for grace.

sentences.zh: 今處之塞內，與民雜居，彼窺郡縣虛實，必為邊患，不如徙之塞外以防未然。

translations.literal: Now if we settle them within the passes to live mixed with the people, they will spy out the truth of commanderies and counties and surely become a frontier calamity. It would be better to relocate them beyond the passes to guard against what has not yet happened."
translations.idiomatic: Settle them inside the passes among our people and they will learn the strength and weakness of every commandery and county. They are sure to become a frontier scourge. Better relocate them beyond the passes before trouble begins."

sentences.zh: 」堅從之。

translations.literal: " Jian followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: " Fu Jian followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 十一月，封桓溫為南郡公，溫弟沖為豐城縣公，子濟為臨賀縣公。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Huan Wen was enfeoffed as Duke of Nan commandery; Wen's younger brother Chong as Duke of Fengcheng county; and Wen's son Ji as Duke of Linhe county.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Huan Wen was enfeoffed as Duke of Nan commandery, his younger brother Huan Chong as Duke of Fengcheng county, and his son Huan Ji as Duke of Linhe county.

sentences.zh: 燕太宰恪欲以李績為右僕射，燕主暐不許。

translations.literal: Yan's Grand Preceptor Ke wished to appoint Li Ji as Right Vice Director; the Yan ruler Wei did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Murong Ke of Yan wished to appoint Li Ji Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, but Emperor Murong Wei refused.

sentences.zh: 恪屢以為請，暐曰：「萬機之事，皆委之叔父，伯陽一人，暐請獨裁。

translations.literal: Ke repeatedly requested it. Wei said: "The myriad affairs of state I entrust entirely to my uncle; for this one man, Boyang, I ask to decide alone.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ke pressed the matter repeatedly. Murong Wei said, "I entrust every affair of state to my uncle. For this one man, Boyang, I ask to decide alone.

sentences.zh: 」出為章武太守，以憂卒。

translations.literal: " Li Ji was sent out as governor of Zhangwu and died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: " Li Ji was sent out as governor of Zhangwu and died of grief.

sentences.zh: 孝宗穆皇帝下升平五年（

translations.literal: The fifth year of Shengping under Emperor Xiaozong Mu (
translations.idiomatic: Fifth year of Shengping, reign of Emperor Xiaozong Mu (

sentences.zh: 辛酉，公元三六一年）

translations.literal: xinyou, AD 361)
translations.idiomatic: xinyou year, AD 361)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，戊戌，大赦。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on wuxu day, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on wuxu day, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 劉衛辰掠秦邊民五十餘口為奴婢以獻於秦；

translations.literal: Liu Weichen seized more than fifty border people of Qin as slaves and presented them to Qin;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Weichen seized more than fifty Qin border people as slaves and presented them to Former Qin;

sentences.zh: 秦王堅責之，使歸所掠。

translations.literal: the Qin king Jian rebuked him and ordered the return of those seized.
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian rebuked him and ordered the captives returned.

sentences.zh: 衛辰由是叛秦，專附於代。

translations.literal: Weichen thereupon rebelled against Qin and attached himself solely to Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Weichen thereupon rebelled against Qin and attached himself solely to Dai.

sentences.zh: 東安簡伯郗曇卒。

translations.literal: Eastern Peace Simple Baron Chi Tan died.
translations.idiomatic: Chi Tan, Baron of Eastern Peace, died.

sentences.zh: 二月，以東陽太守范汪都督徐、兗、青、冀、幽五州諸軍事，兼徐、兗二州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second month, Fan Wang, governor of Dongyang, was made overseer of military affairs for Xu, Yan, Qing, Ji, and You provinces, and concurrently inspector of Xu and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Fan Wang, governor of Dongyang, was appointed commander-in-chief for Xu, Yan, Qing, Ji, and You and concurrently inspector of Xu and Yan.

sentences.zh: 平陽人舉郡降燕。

translations.literal: The people of Pingyang raised the whole commandery in surrender to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Pingyang surrendered the entire commandery to Yan.

sentences.zh: 燕以建威將軍段剛為太守，遣督護韓苞將兵共守平陽。

translations.literal: Yan appointed General Who Establishes Might Duan Gang as governor and sent the overseer Han Bao leading troops jointly to hold Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yan appointed Duan Gang, General Who Establishes Might, governor and sent the overseer Han Bao with troops to hold Pingyang jointly.

sentences.zh: 方士丁進有寵於燕主俊，欲求媚於太宰恪，說恪令殺太傅評；

translations.literal: The adept Ding Jin had favor with the Yan ruler Jun and wished to curry favor with Grand Preceptor Ke; he urged Ke to kill Grand Tutor Ping;
translations.idiomatic: The wonder-worker Ding Jin had enjoyed Murong Jun's favor and now sought to please Grand Preceptor Murong Ke by urging him to kill Grand Tutor Murong Ping;

sentences.zh: 恪大怒，奏收斬之。

translations.literal: Ke was greatly angered and memorialized to seize and execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ke was furious and memorialized for his arrest and execution.

sentences.zh: 高昌卒，燕河內太守呂護並其眾，遣使來降；

translations.literal: Gao Chang died; Yan's governor of Henei, Lü Hu, absorbed his forces and sent envoys to come over in surrender;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Chang died. Lü Hu, governor of Henei for Yan, absorbed his forces and sent envoys to surrender;

sentences.zh: 拜護冀州刺史。

translations.literal: Hu was appointed inspector of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Hu was appointed inspector of Ji.

sentences.zh: 護欲引晉兵以襲鄴。

translations.literal: Hu wished to bring in Jin troops to strike Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Hu wished to bring Jin troops against Ye.

sentences.zh: 三月，燕太宰恪將兵五萬，冠軍將軍皇甫真將兵萬人，共討之。

translations.literal: In the third month, Yan's Grand Preceptor Ke led fifty thousand troops and Champion General Huangfu Zhen led ten thousand; together they attacked him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Grand Preceptor Murong Ke led fifty thousand men and Champion General Huangfu Zhen ten thousand to attack him together.

sentences.zh: 燕兵至野王，護嬰城自守。

translations.literal: The Yan army reached Yewang; Hu shut the city and held it.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan army reached Yewang. Lü Hu shut the city and defended it.

sentences.zh: 護軍將軍傅顏請急攻之，以省大費。

translations.literal: Protector of the Army Fu Yan requested a rapid assault to save great expense.
translations.idiomatic: Protector of the Army Fu Yan urged a swift assault to spare great expense.

sentences.zh: 恪曰：「老賊經變多矣，觀其守備，未易猝攻。

translations.literal: Ke said: "This old rebel has seen many changes; judging by his defenses, he is not easy to assault suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ke said, "This old rebel has weathered many turns of fortune. Judging by his defenses, he cannot be taken in a rush.

sentences.zh: 頃攻黎陽，多殺精銳，卒不能拔，自取困辱。

translations.literal: Recently in attacking Liyang we killed many elite troops yet in the end could not take it—we brought trouble and shame on ourselves."
translations.idiomatic: When we attacked Liyang not long ago we slaughtered many of our best men and still could not take the place. We only brought trouble and shame on ourselves."

sentences.zh: 護內無蓄積，外無救援，我深溝高壘，坐而守之，休兵養士，離間其黨，於我不勞而賊勢日蹙。

translations.literal: Within, Hu has no stores; without, no rescue. We shall dig deep moats and raise high ramparts, sit and hold them, rest the troops and nourish the soldiers, sow discord among his partisans—without labor on our part the rebel's strength will daily tighten.
translations.idiomatic: Hu has no stores within and no rescue without. We shall dig deep moats, raise high ramparts, and hold our ground. We will rest the troops, nourish the men, and sow discord among his partisans. Without exhausting ourselves we shall see the rebel's strength daily tighten.

sentences.zh: 不過十旬，取之必矣，何為多殺士卒以求旦夕之功乎！

translations.literal: In no more than ten ten-day periods we are sure to take him—why slaughter many soldiers to seek a moment's achievement!
translations.idiomatic: In less than a hundred days we are sure to take him. Why slaughter soldiers for a moment's glory?

sentences.zh: 」乃築長圍守之。

translations.literal: " He then built a long encirclement and besieged the city.
translations.idiomatic: " He then built a long encirclement and laid siege.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，桓溫以其弟黃門郎豁督沔中七郡諸軍事，兼新野、義城二郡太守，將兵取許昌，破燕將慕容塵。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Huan Wen had his younger brother, the Yellow Gate Attendant Huo, oversee military affairs for the seven commanderies of Mianzhong and concurrently serve as governor of Xinye and Yicheng, leading troops to take Xuchang and defeating the Yan general Murong Chen.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Huan Wen appointed his younger brother Huan Huo, Yellow Gate Attendant, commander for the seven Mianzhong commanderies and concurrently governor of Xinye and Yicheng. Huan Huo led troops to take Xuchang and defeated the Yan general Murong Chen.

sentences.zh: 涼驃騎大將軍宋混疾甚，弦玄靚及其祖母馬氏往省之，曰：「將軍萬一不幸，寡婦孤兒將何所托！

translations.literal: Former Liang's General of Agile Cavalry Song Hun was gravely ill. Zhang Xuanjing and his grandmother, Lady Ma, went to visit him and said: "If the general should meet misfortune, to whom will the widow and orphan be entrusted!
translations.idiomatic: Song Hun, General of Agile Cavalry of Former Liang, fell gravely ill. Zhang Xuanjing and his grandmother Lady Ma visited him and said, "If the general should not recover, to whom shall the widow and orphan entrust themselves?

sentences.zh: 欲以林宗繼將軍，可乎？

translations.literal: We wish to have Linzong succeed the general—is that acceptable?
translations.idiomatic: We wish to have Linzong succeed you. Would that be acceptable?

sentences.zh: 」混曰；

translations.literal: " Hun said:
translations.idiomatic: " Song Hun said,

sentences.zh: 「臣子林宗幼弱，不堪大任。

translations.literal: "My son Linzong is young and weak and cannot bear great responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: "My son Linzong is young and weak and cannot bear great responsibility.

sentences.zh: 殿下倘未棄臣門，臣弟澄政事愈於臣，但恐其儒緩，機事不稱耳。

translations.literal: If Your Highness has not yet abandoned my house, my younger brother Cheng is superior to me in government affairs, but I fear he is scholarly and slow and may not suit urgent affairs.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Highness has not yet abandoned our house, my younger brother Cheng surpasses me in government, though I fear he is scholarly and slow and may not suit urgent affairs.

sentences.zh: 殿下策勵而使之，可也。

translations.literal: If Your Highness urges and encourages him to serve, it will do.
translations.idiomatic: Urge and encourage him, and he will serve well enough.

sentences.zh: 」混戒澄及諸子曰：「吾家受國大恩，當以死報，無恃勢位以驕人。

translations.literal: " Hun admonished Cheng and his other sons: "Our house has received great grace from the state and must repay it with death. Do not rely on power and position to be arrogant toward others.
translations.idiomatic: " Song Hun admonished Cheng and his other sons: "Our house has received great grace from the state and must repay it with our lives. Do not rely on power and position to lord it over others.

sentences.zh: 」又見朝臣，皆戒之以忠貞。

translations.literal: " He also saw court ministers and admonished them all to loyalty and steadfastness.
translations.idiomatic: " He also saw court ministers and admonished them all to loyalty and steadfastness.

sentences.zh: 及卒，行路為之揮涕。

translations.literal: When he died, travelers along the road wept for him.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, travelers along the road wept for him.

sentences.zh: 雲靚以澄為領軍將軍，輔政。

translations.literal: Xuanjing appointed Cheng Palace Guard general to assist in government.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xuanjing appointed Song Cheng Palace Guard general to assist in government.

sentences.zh: 五月，丁巳，帝崩，無嗣。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on dingsi day, the emperor died without an heir.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on dingsi day, the emperor died without an heir.

sentences.zh: 皇太后令曰：「琅邪王丕，中興正統，義望情地，莫與為比，其以王奉大統！

translations.literal: The empress dowager issued an order: "The Prince of Langye, Pi, is the legitimate line of the Restoration; in righteousness, reputation, and kinship none can compare—let the prince receive the great succession!
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager issued an order: "Sima Pi, Prince of Langye, is the legitimate heir of the Restoration. In righteousness, reputation, and kinship none can compare. Let him receive the throne!

sentences.zh: 」於是百官備法駕迎於琅邪第。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the hundred officials prepared the imperial equipage and welcomed him at the Langye residence.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon the officials prepared the imperial equipage and welcomed him at the Langye residence.

sentences.zh: 庚申，即皇帝位，大赦。

translations.literal: On gengshen day he ascended the imperial throne and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen day he ascended the throne and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，改封東海王弈為琅邪王。

translations.literal: On renxu day the Prince of Donghai, Yi, was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu day Sima Yi, Prince of Donghai, was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Langye.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，戊午，葬穆帝於永平陵，廟號孝宗。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on wuwu day, Emperor Mu was buried at Yongping tomb; his temple name was Xiaozong.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on wuwu day, Emperor Mu was buried at Yongping tomb. His temple name was Xiaozong.

sentences.zh: 燕人圍野王數月，呂護遣其將張興出戰，傅顏擊斬之，城中日蹙。

translations.literal: The Yan besieged Yewang for several months. Lü Hu sent his general Zhang Xing out to battle; Fu Yan struck and beheaded him, and within the city the situation daily tightened.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan besieged Yewang for months. Lü Hu sent his general Zhang Xing out to fight; Fu Yan struck and killed him, and the city's plight grew daily worse.

sentences.zh: 皇甫真戒部將曰：「護勢窮奔突，必擇虛隙而投之；

translations.literal: Huangfu Zhen warned his subordinate generals: "When Hu is cornered and dashes about, he is sure to choose a weak gap and throw himself at it;
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Zhen warned his officers: "When Hu is cornered he will dash about and strike wherever he finds a weak gap.

sentences.zh: 吾所部士卒多羸，器甲不精，宜深為之備。

translations.literal: the troops under my command are mostly weak, and their arms and armor are not fine—you ought to prepare deeply for this.
translations.idiomatic: My troops are mostly weak and their arms and armor poor. You must prepare thoroughly.

sentences.zh: 」乃多課櫓楯，親察行夜者。

translations.literal: " He then levied many siege towers and shields and personally inspected the night patrol.
translations.idiomatic: " He then levied many siege towers and shields and personally inspected the night patrol.

sentences.zh: 護食盡，果夜悉精銳趨真所部，突圍，不得出；

translations.literal: When Hu's food was exhausted, he indeed led all his elite by night toward Zhen's command to break out but could not get out;
translations.idiomatic: When Hu's food ran out, he led all his elite by night against Huangfu Zhen's sector to break out but could not escape.

sentences.zh: 太宰恪引兵擊之，護眾死傷殆盡，棄妻子奔滎陽。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor Ke led troops to strike him; Hu's host was nearly all killed or wounded, and he abandoned wife and children and fled to Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Murong Ke led troops against him. Hu's force was nearly annihilated. He abandoned wife and children and fled to Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 恪存撫降民，給其廩食；

translations.literal: Ke comforted and cared for the surrendered people and gave them grain rations;
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ke comforted the surrendered people and gave them grain rations.

sentences.zh: 徙士人、將帥於鄴，自餘各隨所樂。

translations.literal: he relocated gentry and commanders to Ye; the rest each followed their own preference.
translations.idiomatic: He relocated scholars and commanders to Ye; the rest went wherever they wished.

sentences.zh: 以護參軍廣平梁琛為中書著作郎。

translations.literal: He appointed Lü Hu's staff officer Liang Chen of Guangping as Secretariat drafting officer.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Liang Chen of Guangping, a staff officer of Lü Hu, drafting officer of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 九月，戊申，立妃王氏為皇后。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on wushen day, Consort Wang was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on wushen day, Consort Wang was established as empress.

sentences.zh: -{后}-，濛之女也。

translations.literal: The empress was the daughter of Meng.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was the daughter of Wang Meng.

sentences.zh: 穆帝何皇后稱穆皇后，居永安宮。

translations.literal: Empress He of Emperor Mu was styled Empress Mu and resided in Yong'an Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Empress He, widow of Emperor Mu, took the title Empress Mu and resided in Yong'an Palace.

sentences.zh: 涼右司馬張邕惡宋澄專政，起兵攻澄，殺之，並滅其族。

translations.literal: Former Liang's Right Major Zhang Yong hated Song Cheng's monopoly of government, raised troops to attack Cheng, killed him, and exterminated his clan as well.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yong, Right Major of Former Liang, hated Song Cheng's monopoly of power. He raised troops, killed Cheng, and exterminated his clan.

sentences.zh: 張玄靚以邕為中護軍，叔父天錫為中領軍，同輔政。

translations.literal: Zhang Xuanjing appointed Yong Central Guard general and his uncle Tiansi Central Army general; together they assisted in government.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xuanjing appointed Zhang Yong Central Guard general and his uncle Zhang Tiansi Central Army general to assist in government together.

sentences.zh: 張平襲燕平陽，殺段剛、韓苞；

translations.literal: Zhang Ping raided Yan's Pingyang, killing Duan Gang and Han Bao;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ping raided Pingyang in Yan territory and killed Duan Gang and Han Bao.

sentences.zh: 又攻雁門，殺太守單男。

translations.literal: he also attacked Yanmen and killed the governor Shan Nan.
translations.idiomatic: He also attacked Yanmen and killed the governor Shan Nan.

sentences.zh: 既而為秦所攻，平復謝罪於燕以求救。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was attacked by Qin; Ping again apologized to Yan to seek rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Qin attacked him. Zhang Ping apologized to Yan and sought rescue.

sentences.zh: 燕人以平反覆，弗救也，平遂為秦所滅。

translations.literal: The Yan considered Ping treacherous and did not rescue him; Ping was thereupon destroyed by Qin.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan considered Zhang Ping treacherous and refused to help. Qin destroyed him.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，秦大赦。

translations.literal: On yihai day Qin proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai day Former Qin proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 徐、兗二州刺史范汪，素為桓溫所惡，溫將北伐，命汪帥眾出梁國。

translations.literal: Fan Wang, inspector of Xu and Yan, had long been hated by Huan Wen. When Wen was about to campaign north, he ordered Wang to lead troops out through Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Wang, inspector of Xu and Yan, had long been hated by Huan Wen. When Wen prepared his northern campaign he ordered Wang to lead troops through Liang.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，坐失期，免為庶人，遂廢，卒於家。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, for missing the deadline he was dismissed to commoner status, then deposed, and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, for missing the deadline he was reduced to commoner status, deposed, and died at home.

sentences.zh: 子寧，好儒學，性質直，常謂王弼、何晏之罪深於桀、紂。

translations.literal: His son Ning loved Confucian learning and was upright by nature; he often said the crimes of Wang Bi and He Yan were deeper than those of Jie and Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fan Ning loved Confucian learning and was upright by nature. He often said the crimes of Wang Bi and He Yan were deeper than those of Jie and Zhou.

sentences.zh: 或以為貶之太過。

translations.literal: Some thought this condemnation excessive.
translations.idiomatic: Some thought this condemnation excessive.

sentences.zh: 寧曰：「王、何蔑棄典文，幽沈仁義，游辭浮說，波蕩後生，使搢紳之徒翻然改轍，以至禮壞樂崩，中原傾覆，遺風餘俗，至今為患。

translations.literal: Ning said: "Wang and He despised and abandoned the canonical texts, buried benevolence and righteousness, wandered in empty words and floating doctrines, and stirred the young generation, causing gentlemen to turn their carriage tracks—until rites were ruined and music collapsed, the Central Plains overturned, and the lingering customs remain a calamity to this day.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ning said, "Wang and He despised the canonical texts, buried benevolence and righteousness, trafficked in empty words, and misled the young. Gentlemen turned from the old ways until rites collapsed and music failed, the Central Plains fell, and their poisoned customs plague us still.

sentences.zh: 桀、紂縱暴一時，適足以喪身覆國，為後世戒，豈能回百姓之視聽哉！

translations.literal: Jie and Zhou indulged violence for a season, sufficient only to lose their persons and overturn their states as a warning to later ages—how could they turn the eyes and ears of the common people!
translations.idiomatic: Jie and Zhou were violent for a season and lost only themselves and their states, a warning to later ages. How could they turn the eyes and ears of the people?

sentences.zh: 故吾以為一世之禍輕，歷代之患重，自喪之惡小，迷眾之罪大也。

translations.literal: Therefore I hold that the calamity of one age is light while the affliction of successive ages is heavy; the evil of self-destruction is small while the crime of misleading the multitude is great."
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I hold that the harm of one age is light and the harm of many ages heavy; the evil of self-destruction small and the crime of misleading the multitude great."

sentences.zh: 呂護復叛，奔燕，燕人赦之，以為廣州刺史。

translations.literal: Lü Hu rebelled again, fled to Yan, and the Yan pardoned him and appointed him inspector of Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Hu rebelled again and fled to Yan. The Yan pardoned him and appointed him inspector of Guang.

sentences.zh: 涼張邕驕矜淫縱，樹黨專權，多所刑殺，國人患之。

translations.literal: Zhang Yong of Liang was arrogant, harsh, licentious, and unrestrained; he built factions and monopolized power, executed many, and the people of the state resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yong of Former Liang was arrogant, licentious, and cruel. He built factions, monopolized power, and executed many. The people hated him.

sentences.zh: 張天錫所親敦煌劉肅謂天錫曰：「國家事欲未靜！

translations.literal: Liu Su of Dunhuang, whom Zhang Tiansi favored, said to Tiansi: "Affairs of state and family are about to be unsettled!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Su of Dunhuang, a favorite of Zhang Tiansi, said to him, "State and family are about to be thrown into turmoil!

sentences.zh: 」天錫曰：「何謂也？

translations.literal: " Tiansi said: "What do you mean?
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang Tiansi said, "What do you mean?

sentences.zh: 」肅曰：「今護軍出入，有似長寧。

translations.literal: " Su said: "The Protector of the Army coming and going now resembles Changning."
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Su said, "The Protector of the Army now comes and goes like Changning."

sentences.zh: 」天錫驚曰：「我固疑之，未敢出口。

translations.literal: " Tiansi said in alarm: "I have long suspected this but dared not speak it aloud.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang Tiansi said in alarm, "I have long suspected this but dared not speak aloud.

sentences.zh: 計將安出？

translations.literal: What plan can we devise?
translations.idiomatic: What is to be done?

sentences.zh: 」肅曰：「正當速除之耳！

translations.literal: " Su said: "We should simply remove him quickly!"
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Su said, "We must remove him at once!"

sentences.zh: 」天錫曰：「安得其人？

translations.literal: " Tiansi said: "Where can we get the man?
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang Tiansi said, "Where shall we find the man?

sentences.zh: 」肅曰：「肅即其人也！

translations.literal: " Su said: "Su is the man!"
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Su said, "I am the man!"

sentences.zh: 」肅時年未二十。

translations.literal: " Su was not yet twenty.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Su was not yet twenty.

sentences.zh: 天錫曰：「汝年少，更求其助。

translations.literal: Tiansi said: "You are young—seek further help.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tiansi said, "You are young. Find more help.

sentences.zh: 」肅曰：「趙白駒與肅二人足矣。

translations.literal: " Su said: "Zhao Baiju and Su, two men, are enough."
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Su said, "Zhao Baiju and I are enough."

sentences.zh: 」十一月，天錫與邕俱入朝，肅與白駒從天錫，值邕於門下，肅斫之不中，白駒繼之，又不克，二人與天錫俱入宮中，邕得逸走，帥甲士三百餘人攻宮門。

translations.literal: " In the eleventh month Tiansi and Yong both entered court; Su and Baiju followed Tiansi. They met Yong at the gate; Su struck at him and missed, Baiju followed and also failed. The two men entered the palace with Tiansi. Yong escaped, gathered more than three hundred armored soldiers, and attacked the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: " In the eleventh month Zhang Tiansi and Zhang Yong both entered court. Liu Su and Zhao Baiju followed Tiansi. At the gate Su struck at Yong and missed; Baiju struck again and failed. The two entered the palace with Tiansi. Yong escaped, gathered more than three hundred armored men, and attacked the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 天錫登屋大呼曰：「張邕凶逆無道，既滅宋氏，又欲傾覆我家。

translations.literal: Tiansi mounted the roof and shouted: "Zhang Yong is vicious, rebellious, and without the Way. Having destroyed the Song house, he now wishes to overturn our house as well.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tiansi mounted the roof and shouted, "Zhang Yong is vicious and lawless. Having destroyed the Song house, he now wishes to overturn ours.

sentences.zh: 汝將士世為涼臣，何忍以兵相向邪！

translations.literal: You officers and soldiers have for generations been subjects of Liang—how can you bear to turn weapons on one another!
translations.idiomatic: You officers and soldiers have served Liang for generations. How can you turn weapons on one another?

sentences.zh: 今所取者，止張邕耳，它無所問！

translations.literal: What we seek now is only Zhang Yong; nothing else will be asked!
translations.idiomatic: We seek only Zhang Yong. No one else will be punished!

sentences.zh: 」於是邕兵悉散走，邕自刎死，盡滅其族黨。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Yong's soldiers all scattered and fled; Yong killed himself by the sword, and his clan and partisans were utterly destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: " Yong's soldiers scattered. Yong killed himself, and his clan and partisans were utterly destroyed.

sentences.zh: 玄靚以天錫為使持節、冠軍大將軍、都督中外諸軍事，輔政。

translations.literal: Xuanjing appointed Tiansi bearer of the staff of authority, Champion Grand General, and overseer of all military affairs within and without, to assist in government.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xuanjing appointed Zhang Tiansi bearer of the staff of authority, Champion Grand General, and commander of all forces at court and in the field to assist in government.

sentences.zh: 十二月，始改建興四十九年，奉升平年號，詔以玄靚為大都督、督隴右諸軍事、涼州刺史、護羌校尉、西平公。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month they first changed from the forty-ninth year of Jianxing and adopted the Shengping era name. An edict appointed Xuanjing Grand Commander, overseer of military affairs for Longyou, inspector of Liang, Protector of the Qiang, and Duke of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Liang first abandoned the forty-ninth year of Jianxing and adopted the Jin era name Shengping. An edict appointed Zhang Xuanjing Grand Commander, commander for Longyou, inspector of Liang, Protector of the Qiang, and Duke of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 燕大赦。

translations.literal: Yan proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Yan proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅命牧伯守宰各舉孝悌、廉直、文學、政事，察其所舉，得人者賞之，非其人者罪之。

translations.literal: The Qin king Jian ordered regional chiefs and district governors each to recommend men of filial piety and brotherly respect, integrity and uprightness, literary learning, and administrative ability; he would examine their recommendations—rewarding those who obtained the right men and punishing those who did not.
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian ordered regional chiefs and district governors each to recommend men of filial piety, integrity, literary learning, and administrative ability. He would examine their choices, reward those who found good men, and punish those who did not.

sentences.zh: 由是人莫敢妄舉，而請托不行，士皆自勵；

translations.literal: From this no one dared recommend rashly; patronage requests did not succeed; and scholars all encouraged themselves;
translations.idiomatic: From this no one dared recommend rashly, patronage failed, and scholars strove to improve themselves.

sentences.zh: 雖宗室外戚，無才能者皆棄不用。

translations.literal: even among the imperial clan and maternal kin, those without ability were all discarded and not employed.
translations.idiomatic: Even among the imperial clan and maternal kin, the incapable were set aside.

sentences.zh: 當是之時，內外之官，率皆稱職；

translations.literal: At this time, officials within and without were for the most part equal to their posts;
translations.idiomatic: At this time officials within and without were for the most part equal to their posts.

sentences.zh: 田疇修辟，倉庫充實，盜賊屏息。

translations.literal: fields and pastures were cultivated and opened, storehouses full, and bandits silenced.
translations.idiomatic: Fields were cultivated, storehouses full, and bandits silenced.

sentences.zh: 是歲，歸義侯李勢卒。

translations.literal: In this year the Marquis of Guiyi, Li Shi, died.
translations.idiomatic: In this year Li Shi, Marquis of Guiyi, died.

sentences.zh: 孝宗穆皇帝下隆和元年（

translations.literal: The first year of Longhe under Emperor Xiaozong Mu (
translations.idiomatic: First year of Longhe, reign of Emperor Xiaozong Mu (

sentences.zh: 壬戌，公元三六二年）

translations.literal: renxu, AD 362)
translations.idiomatic: renxu year, AD 362)

sentences.zh: 春，正有，壬子，大赦，改元。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on renzi day, a general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name changed.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on renzi day, a general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name changed.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，減田租，畝收二升。

translations.literal: On jiayin day land tax was reduced to two sheng per mu.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin day the land tax was reduced to two sheng per mu.

sentences.zh: 燕豫州刺史孫興請攻洛陽，曰：「晉將陳祐弊卒千餘，介守孤城，不中取也！

translations.literal: Yan's inspector of Yu, Sun Xing, requested an attack on Luoyang, saying: "The Jin general Chen You has a thousand-odd worn troops holding a lone city in isolation—it cannot withstand capture!
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xing, inspector of Yu for Yan, urged an attack on Luoyang: "The Jin general Chen You holds the lone city with a thousand worn troops. It cannot stand!"

sentences.zh: 」燕人從其言，遣寧南將軍呂護屯河陰。

translations.literal: " The Yan followed his advice and sent the General Who Pacifies the South, Lü Hu, to encamp at Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: " The Yan agreed and sent General Who Pacifies the South Lü Hu to encamp at Heyin.

sentences.zh: 二月，辛未，以吳國內史庾希為北中郎將、徐、兗二州刺史，鎮下邳，龍驤將軍袁真為西中郎將、監護豫、司、並、冀四州諸軍事、豫州刺史，鎮汝南並假節。

translations.literal: In the second month, on xinwei day, Yu Xi, interior minister of Wu, was made North Central Commander and inspector of Xu and Yan, stationed at Xiapi; the Dragon Cavalry general Yuan Zhen was made West Central Commander, overseer of military affairs for Yu, Si, Bing, and Ji, and inspector of Yu, stationed at Runan with provisional staff of authority.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on xinwei day, Yu Xi, interior minister of Wu, was appointed North Central Commander and inspector of Xu and Yan, stationed at Xiapi. Dragon Cavalry general Yuan Zhen was appointed West Central Commander, commander for Yu, Si, Bing, and Ji, and inspector of Yu, stationed at Runan with provisional staff of authority.

sentences.zh: 希，冰之子也。

translations.literal: Xi was the son of Bing.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xi was the son of Yu Bing.

sentences.zh: 丙子，拜帝母周貴人為皇太妃，儀服擬於太后。

translations.literal: On bingzi day the emperor's mother, Lady Zhou, was honored as imperial consort dowager, her ritual and regalia matching the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi day the emperor's mother, Lady Zhou, was honored as imperial consort dowager with ritual and regalia matching the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 燕呂護攻洛陽。

translations.literal: Lü Hu of Yan attacked Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Hu of Yan attacked Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 三月，乙酉，河南太守戴施奔宛，陳祐告急。

translations.literal: In the third month, on yiyou day, Dai Shi, governor of Henan, fled to Wan; Chen You reported urgent distress.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on yiyou day, Dai Shi, governor of Henan, fled to Wan. Chen You sent urgent appeals for help.

sentences.zh: 五月，丁巳，桓溫遣庾希及竟陵太守鄧遐帥舟師三千人助祐守洛陽，遐。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on dingsi day, Huan Wen sent Yu Xi and Deng Xia, governor of Jingling, leading three thousand men in river craft to help You hold Luoyang. Xia
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on dingsi day, Huan Wen sent Yu Xi and Deng Xia, governor of Jingling, with three thousand men in river craft to help Chen You hold Luoyang. Deng Xia

sentences.zh: 岳之子也。

translations.literal: was the son of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: was the son of Deng Yue.

sentences.zh: 溫上疏請遷都洛陽。

translations.literal: Wen memorialized requesting that the capital be moved to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen memorialized requesting that the capital be moved to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 自永嘉之亂播渡江表者，一切北徙，以實河南。

translations.literal: All who since the Yongjia turmoil had scattered south of the river were to move north to fill Henan.
translations.idiomatic: All who since the Yongjia turmoil had fled south of the Yangzi were to move north to fill Henan.

sentences.zh: 朝廷畏溫，不敢為異。

translations.literal: The court feared Wen and dared not dissent.
translations.idiomatic: The court feared Huan Wen and dared not dissent.

sentences.zh: 而北土蕭條，人情疑懼，雖並知不可，莫敢先諫。

translations.literal: Yet the northern lands were desolate; men's hearts were doubtful and afraid; although all knew it could not be done, none dared remonstrate first.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the north was desolate and men were fearful. Though all knew the plan was impossible, none dared speak first.

sentences.zh: 散騎常待領著作郎孫綽上疏曰：「昔中宗龍飛，非惟信順協於天人，實賴萬里長江畫而守之耳。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Sun Chuo, who also headed the History Office, memorialized: "In former times when Emperor Zhongzong ascended the dragon throne, it was not only that trust and compliance harmonized heaven and man—he truly relied on the ten-thousand-li Yangzi, drawn as a boundary and guarded.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Sun Chuo, who also headed the History Office, memorialized: "When Emperor Zhongzong ascended the throne, it was not only that trust and compliance harmonized heaven and man. He truly relied on the ten-thousand-li Yangzi as a drawn boundary to guard the realm.

sentences.zh: 今自喪亂已來，六十餘年，河、洛丘墟，函夏蕭條。

translations.literal: Now since the disorders began, more than sixty years have passed; the Yellow River and Luo are ruins, and within the passes all is desolate.
translations.idiomatic: Since the disorders began more than sixty years have passed. The Yellow River and Luo are ruins, and the heartland is desolate.

sentences.zh: 士民播流江表，已經數世，存者老子長孫，亡者丘隴成行，雖北風之思感其素心，目前之哀實為交切。

translations.literal: Gentry and commoners have scattered to the lands beyond the river for several generations; the living have grown old and raised grandsons, the dead lie in rows of mounds. Though thoughts of the northern wind touch their native hearts, the grief before their eyes is truly pressing and keen.
translations.idiomatic: Gentry and commoners have lived beyond the river for generations. The living have grown old and raised grandsons; the dead lie in rows of mounds. Though longing for the north still stirs their hearts, the grief before their eyes is immediate and keen.

sentences.zh: 若遷都旋軫之日，中興五陵，即復緬成遐域。

translations.literal: If on the day the capital turns its wheels to move, the five tombs of the Restoration would at once again become distant borderlands.
translations.idiomatic: If the capital wheels turn northward, the five tombs of the Restoration would at once become distant borderlands again.

sentences.zh: 秦山之安，既難以理保，烝烝之思，豈不纏於聖心哉！

translations.literal: The security of Mount Tai would be hard to preserve by reason; would not the people's yearning twine about the sage heart!
translations.idiomatic: The security of Mount Tai would be hard to preserve by reason alone. Would not the people's yearning twine about Your Majesty's heart?

sentences.zh: 溫今此舉，誠欲大覽始終，為國遠圖；

translations.literal: Wen's present move truly wishes to survey beginning and end in the large view and make distant plans for the state;
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen's present move truly aims to survey the whole course of affairs and plan far ahead for the state.

sentences.zh: 而百姓震駭，同懷危懼，豈不以反舊之樂賒，而趨死之憂促哉！

translations.literal: yet the common people are shaken and terrified, all sharing peril and fear—is it not because the joy of returning to the old is distant while the dread of rushing toward death is pressing!
translations.idiomatic: Yet the people are shaken and terrified, all sharing peril and fear. Is it not because the joy of returning home is distant while the dread of rushing toward death is pressing?

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 植根江外，數十年矣，一朝頓欲拔之，驅踧於窮荒之地。

translations.literal: They have taken root beyond the river for several decades; in a single morning you would suddenly uproot them and drive them in haste to barren and distant lands.
translations.idiomatic: They have taken root beyond the river for decades. In a single morning you would uproot them and drive them in haste to barren and distant lands.

sentences.zh: 提挈萬里，逾險浮深，離墳墓，棄生業，田宅不可復售，舟車無從而得。

translations.literal: To drag them ten thousand li, cross dangers and float over deep waters, leave graves and tombs, abandon their livelihoods—fields and houses cannot be sold again, boats and carts cannot be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: They would be dragged ten thousand li, crossing dangers and deep waters, leaving graves and tombs and abandoning their livelihoods. Fields and houses could not be sold again, and boats and carts could not be obtained.

sentences.zh: 捨安樂之國，適習亂之鄉，將頓僕道塗，飄溺江川，僅有達者。

translations.literal: They would abandon a land of peace and joy for a region accustomed to disorder; many would collapse and fall on the roads, drown adrift in rivers—only a few would arrive.
translations.idiomatic: They would leave a land of peace and ease for a region accustomed to disorder. Many would collapse on the roads or drown in the rivers; only a few would survive the journey.

sentences.zh: 此仁者所宜哀矜，國家所宜深慮也！

translations.literal: This is what the humane should pity, and what the state should deeply weigh!
translations.idiomatic: This is what the humane should pity, and what the state should weigh with the deepest care!

sentences.zh: 臣之愚計，以為且宜遣將帥有威名、資實者，先鎮洛陽，掃平梁、許，清壹河南。

translations.literal: Your servant's humble plan is to think one should first send generals with renown and proven merit to hold Luoyang, sweep clear Liang and Xu, and unify the region south of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant's humble plan is that we should first send generals of proven renown and merit to hold Luoyang, sweep clear Liang and Xu, and restore order south of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 運漕之路既通，開墾之積已豐，豺狼遠竄，中夏小康，然後可徐議遷徙耳。

translations.literal: Once grain-transport routes are open and reclaimed fields have piled up in abundance, wolves and bandits have fled far off, and the Central Plain knows small peace, then one may slowly discuss resettlement.
translations.idiomatic: Once grain routes are open, reclaimed fields abound, bandits have fled far off, and the Central Plain enjoys modest peace, then we may discuss migration at leisure.

sentences.zh: 奈何捨百勝之長理，舉天下而一擲哉！

translations.literal: How could one abandon the long-tested principles of a hundred victories and stake the whole realm on a single throw!
translations.idiomatic: How can we abandon the long-tested principles of steady success and stake the whole realm on a single throw!

sentences.zh: 」綽，楚之孫也。

translations.literal: " Chuo was a grandson of the Chu line.
translations.idiomatic: " Chuo was a grandson of the Chu family.

sentences.zh: 少慕高尚，嘗著《遂初賦》以見志。

translations.literal: From youth he admired high and pure ideals; he once wrote the "Suichu Fu" to express his aims.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he admired loftiness and integrity and once wrote his "Suichu Fu" to declare his aims.

sentences.zh: 溫見綽表，不悅，曰：「致意興公，何不尋君《遂初賦》，而知人家國事邪！

translations.literal: When Wen saw Chuo's memorial he was displeased and said, "Send my regards to Lord Xing—why does he not search out your Suichu Fu and thereby understand other people's state affairs!
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Wen saw Chuo's memorial he was displeased and said, "Send my regards to Lord Xing. Why does he not reread his Suichu Fu and learn what others think of state affairs!

sentences.zh: 時朝廷憂懼，將遣侍中止溫，揚州刺史王述曰：「溫欲以虛聲威朝廷耳，非事實也；

translations.literal: At the time the court was anxious and afraid and was about to send a Gentleman Attendant to stop Wen. The Inspector of Yang Province Wang Shu said, "Wen only wants to use empty threats to awe the court—it is not a real matter;
translations.idiomatic: At the time the court was anxious and afraid and was about to send a Gentleman Attendant to stop Huan Wen. The Inspector of Yang Province Wang Shu said, "Huan Wen only wants to intimidate the court with empty threats. It is not a real plan.

sentences.zh: 但從之，自無所至。

translations.literal: simply go along with him, and naturally nothing will come of it.
translations.idiomatic: Simply go along with him, and nothing will come of it.

sentences.zh: 」乃詔溫曰：「在昔喪亂，忽涉五紀，戎鍬肆暴，繼襲凶跡，眷言西顧，慨歎盈懷。

translations.literal: " Thereupon an edict was issued to Wen: "In former days since the calamity and disorder, suddenly five sixty-year cycles have been crossed; barbarian weapons ran riot in violence, evil traces succeeding one after another. Turning with longing to the west, sighs and lament fill the breast.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon an edict was issued to Huan Wen: "Since the calamities and disorders of former days, five sixty-year cycles have suddenly passed. Barbarian arms have run riot in succession, and with longing turned westward, our sighs and lament overflow the heart.

sentences.zh: 知欲躬帥三軍，蕩滌氛穢，廓清中畿，光復舊京，非夫外身徇國，孰能若此？

translations.literal: We know you wish personally to lead the three armies, wash away foul miasma, clear the central districts, and restore the old capital—is this not devotion of self to the state? Who else could do so?
translations.idiomatic: We know you wish personally to lead the three armies, purge the land of disorder, clear the central heartland, and restore the old capital. Unless one devotes himself entirely to the state, who could do such a thing?

sentences.zh: 諸所處分，委之高算。

translations.literal: All arrangements to be made we entrust to your superior judgment.
translations.idiomatic: We entrust all arrangements to your superior judgment.

sentences.zh: 但河洛丘墟，所營有廣，經始之勤，致勞懷也。

translations.literal: Only the Yellow River and Luo are ruins; the work planned is vast—the labor of beginning it causes concern in our hearts.
translations.idiomatic: But the Yellow River and Luo region is a wasteland, and the work planned is vast. The labor of setting it in motion weighs heavily on our hearts.

sentences.zh: 」事果不行。

translations.literal: " In the end the matter did not go forward.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end the plan was not carried out.

sentences.zh: 溫又議移洛陽鐘虡。

translations.literal: Wen again proposed moving the bells and stands of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen again proposed moving Luoyang's bells and bell-frames.

sentences.zh: 述曰：「永嘉不競，暫都江左，方當蕩平區宇，旋軫舊京。

translations.literal: Shu said, "Since the Yongjia disaster we could not prevail; we temporarily established the capital in the Jiang-Zuo region. When we are about to sweep the realm clear we shall turn our chariots back to the old capital.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu said, "Since the Yongjia disaster we could not prevail and temporarily made the capital in the lands east of the river. When we sweep the realm clear we shall turn our chariots back to the old capital.

sentences.zh: 若其不爾，宜改遷園陵，不應先事鐘虡！

translations.literal: If it is not so, we should first move the imperial tombs and parks—not first concern ourselves with bells and stands!
translations.idiomatic: If that is not the case, we should first move the imperial tombs and parks—not give priority to bells and bell-frames!

sentences.zh: 」溫乃止。

translations.literal: " Wen then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " Huan Wen then abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以交、廣遼遠，改授溫都督並、司、冀三州；

translations.literal: Because Jiao and Guang were remote and distant, the court changed Wen's commission to Grand Commander over Bing, Si, and Ji provinces;
translations.idiomatic: Because Jiao and Guang were remote, the court transferred Huan Wen's command to Bing, Si, and Ji provinces;

sentences.zh: 溫表辭不受。

translations.literal: Wen memorialized declining and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen memorialized declining and refused the appointment.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅親臨太學，考第諸生經義，與博士講論，自是每月一至焉。

translations.literal: King Fu Jian of Qin personally visited the Imperial Academy, ranked the students in the classics, debated with the academicians, and from then on came once each month.
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian of Qin personally visited the Imperial Academy, ranked the students on the classics, and debated with the academicians; thereafter he came once each month.

sentences.zh: 六月，甲戌，燕征東參軍劉拔刺殺征東將軍、冀州刺史、范陽王友於信都。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on jiaxu day, Liu Ba, staff officer on the Eastern Campaign of Yan, assassinated You, Eastern Campaign General, Inspector of Ji Province, and Prince of Fanyang, at Xindu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on jiaxu day, Liu Ba, staff officer on Yan's Eastern Campaign, assassinated You, Eastern Campaign General, Inspector of Ji Province, and Prince of Fanyang, at Xindu.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，呂護退守小平津，中流矢而卒。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Lü Hu retreated to hold Xiaoping Ford and was struck by a flying arrow and died.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Lü Hu retreated to Xiaoping Ford, was struck by a stray arrow, and died.

sentences.zh: 燕將段崇收軍北渡，屯於野王。

translations.literal: The Yan general Duan Chong gathered his army, crossed north, and encamped at Yewang.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan general Duan Chong gathered his troops, crossed north, and encamped at Yewang.

sentences.zh: 鄧遐進屯新城。

translations.literal: Deng Xia advanced and encamped at Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Xia advanced and encamped at Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 八月，西中郎將袁真進屯汝南，運米五萬斛以饋洛陽。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Western Central General Yuan Zhen advanced and encamped at Runan, transporting fifty thousand hu of grain to supply Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Western Central General Yuan Zhen advanced to Runan and transported fifty thousand hu of grain to supply Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，代王什翼犍納女於燕，燕人亦以女妻之。

translations.literal: In winter, the eleventh month, the Dai king Shiyijian gave a daughter in marriage to Yan, and the Yan people also gave a daughter to marry him.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the eleventh month, the Dai king Shiyijian gave a daughter in marriage to Yan, and the Yan people also gave him a daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 十二月，戊午朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the first day wuwu, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the first day wuwu, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 庾希自下邳退屯山陽，袁真自汝南退屯壽陽。

translations.literal: Yu Xi retreated from Xiapi and encamped at Shanyang; Yuan Zhen retreated from Runan and encamped at Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xi withdrew from Xiapi to Shanyang, and Yuan Zhen withdrew from Runan to Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 孝宗穆皇帝下興寧元年（

translations.literal: The first year of Xingning under Emperor Xiaozong Mu (
translations.idiomatic: First year of Xingning, reign of Emperor Xiaozong Mu (

sentences.zh: 癸亥，公元三六三年）

translations.literal: guihai, AD 363)
translations.idiomatic: guihai year, AD 363)

sentences.zh: 春，二月，己亥，大赦，改元。

translations.literal: In spring, the second month, on jihai day, a general amnesty was granted and the era name was changed.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the second month, on jihai day, a general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name was changed.

sentences.zh: 三月，壬寅，皇太妃周氏薨於琅邪第。

translations.literal: In the third month, on renyin day, the Grand Imperial Consort Lady Zhou died at the Langye residence.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on renyin day, the Grand Imperial Consort Lady Zhou died at the Langye residence.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，帝就第治喪，詔司徒會稽王昱總內外眾務。

translations.literal: On guimao day the Emperor went to the residence to handle mourning; an edict appointed the Minister over the Masses, the Prince of Kuaiji Sima Yu, to oversee all internal and external affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao day the Emperor went to the residence to oversee the mourning rites. An edict appointed the Minister over the Masses, Prince of Kuaiji Sima Yu, to oversee all internal and external affairs.

sentences.zh: 帝欲為太妃服三年，僕射江虨啟：「於禮，應服緦麻。

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to observe three years of mourning for the Grand Consort. The Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Jiang Bin memorialized: "By rites one should wear sackcloth of the thinnest grade.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wished to observe three years of mourning for the Grand Consort. Vice Director Jiang Bin memorialized: "By the rites one should wear the lightest grade of mourning.

sentences.zh: 」又欲降服期，虨曰：「厭屈私情，所以上嚴祖考。

translations.literal: " He also wished to reduce mourning to one year. Bin said, "To suppress and bend private feeling is how one elevates reverence for ancestors and the deceased.
translations.idiomatic: " He also wished to reduce the mourning to one year. Jiang Bin said, "To restrain private feeling is how one upholds reverence for one's ancestors.

sentences.zh: 」乃服緦麻。

translations.literal: " He then wore sackcloth of the thinnest grade.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor then wore the lightest grade of mourning.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，燕寧東將軍慕容忠攻滎陽太守劉遠，遠奔魯陽。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Murong Zhong, Pacifying-Eastern General of Yan, attacked Liu Yuan, Administrator of Xingyang; Yuan fled to Luyang.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Yan's Pacifying-Eastern General Murong Zhong attacked Liu Yuan, Administrator of Xingyang. Liu Yuan fled to Luyang.

sentences.zh: 五月，加征西大將軍桓溫侍中、大司馬、都督中外諸軍、錄尚書事，假黃鉞。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Western Campaign Grand General Huan Wen was further appointed Palace Attendant, Grand Marshal, Grand Commander of All Forces at Home and Abroad, and Recorder of the Masters of Writing Affairs, with the yellow axe conferred as token of authority.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Western Campaign Grand General Huan Wen was further appointed Palace Attendant, Grand Marshal, overall commander of all forces at home and abroad, and Recorder of the Masters of Writing, with the yellow battle-axe conferred as a token of supreme authority.

sentences.zh: 溫以撫軍司馬王坦之為長史。

translations.literal: Wen appointed Wang Tanzhi, Military Affairs Officer of the Pacification Army, Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen appointed Wang Tanzhi, Military Affairs Officer of the Pacification Army, as his Chief Clerk.

sentences.zh: 坦之，述之子也。

translations.literal: Tanzhi was Shu's son.
translations.idiomatic: Tanzhi was the son of Wang Shu.

sentences.zh: 又以征西掾郗超為參軍，王珣為主簿，每事必與二人謀之。

translations.literal: He also appointed Xi Chao of the Western Campaign staff as Aide and Wang Bin as Chief Secretary; on every matter he was sure to consult the two of them.
translations.idiomatic: He also appointed Xi Chao of the Western Campaign staff as Aide and Wang Bin as Chief Secretary, and consulted the two on every matter.

sentences.zh: 府中為之語曰：「髯參軍，短主簿，能令公喜，能令公怒。

translations.literal: Within the headquarters a saying ran: "The bearded Aide, the short Chief Secretary—they can make the Lord rejoice and can make the Lord angry.
translations.idiomatic: At headquarters they said, "The bearded Aide and the short Chief Secretary—they can make the Lord rejoice and make the Lord angry.

sentences.zh: 」溫氣概高邁，罕有所推。

translations.literal: " Wen's bearing was lofty and bold; he rarely esteemed anyone.
translations.idiomatic: " Huan Wen's bearing was lofty and bold, and he rarely esteemed anyone.

sentences.zh: 與超言，常自謂不能測，傾身待之，超亦深自結納。

translations.literal: Speaking with Chao, he often said he could not fathom him and leaned his whole person in treating him; Chao also deeply bound himself in loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: In speaking with Xi Chao he often said he could not fathom him and gave himself entirely to honoring him; Chao also devoted himself deeply to him.

sentences.zh: 珣，導之孫也，與謝玄皆為溫掾，溫俱重之。

translations.literal: Bin was the grandson of Wang Dao; he and Xie Xuan were both on Wen's staff, and Wen held both in high regard.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bin was the grandson of Wang Dao. He and Xie Xuan both served on Huan Wen's staff, and Huan Wen held both in high regard.

sentences.zh: 曰：「謝掾年四十必擁旄杖節，王掾當作黑頭公，皆未易才也。

translations.literal: He said, "At forty Staff Officer Xie will surely bear banners and tally; Staff Officer Wang will become a black-haired elder lord—both are talents not easily matched.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "At forty Staff Officer Xie will surely command armies with banner and tally; Staff Officer Wang will become a chief who dies with his hair still black—both are men not easily matched in talent.

sentences.zh: 」玄，奕之子也。

translations.literal: " Xuan was Yi's son.
translations.idiomatic: " Xie Xuan was the son of Xie Yi.

sentences.zh: 以西中郎將袁真都督司、冀、並三州諸軍事，北中郎將庾希都督青州諸軍事。

translations.literal: Western Central General Yuan Zhen was made Grand Commander of military affairs for Si, Ji, and Bing provinces; Northern Central General Yu Xi was made Grand Commander of military affairs for Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Western Central General Yuan Zhen was appointed overall commander of military affairs for Si, Ji, and Bing provinces; Northern Central General Yu Xi was appointed overall commander of military affairs for Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，燕人拔密城，劉遠奔江陵。

translations.literal: On guimao day the Yan forces took Micheng; Liu Yuan fled to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao day the Yan forces took Micheng. Liu Yuan fled to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，有星孛於角、亢。

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, a comet appeared at Jiao and Kang.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the eighth month, a comet appeared in the Horn and Neck constellations.
