sentences.zh: 張玄靚祖母氏卒，尊庶母郭氏為太妃。

translations.literal: Zhang Xuanjing's grandmother the Lady Shi died; he honored his secondary mother Lady Guo as Grand Consort.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xuanjing's grandmother Lady Shi died. He honored his secondary mother Lady Guo as Grand Consort.

sentences.zh: 郭氏以張天錫專政，與大臣張欽等謀誅之。

translations.literal: Lady Guo, because Zhang Tianshi monopolized government, plotted with the high minister Zhang Qin and others to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zhang Tianshi monopolized power, Lady Guo plotted with the high minister Zhang Qin and others to kill him.

sentences.zh: 事洩，欽等皆死。

translations.literal: The plot leaked out; Qin and the others all died.
translations.idiomatic: The plot was discovered and Zhang Qin and the others were all executed.

sentences.zh: 玄靚懼，以位讓天錫，天錫不受。

translations.literal: Xuanjing, in fear, offered the throne to Tianshi; Tianshi did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanjing, in fear, offered the throne to Tianshi, but Tianshi refused.

sentences.zh: 右將軍劉肅等勸天錫自立。

translations.literal: Right General Liu Su and others urged Tianshi to set himself up as ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Right General Liu Su and others urged Tianshi to seize the throne.

sentences.zh: 閏月，天錫使肅等夜帥兵入宮，弒玄靚，宣言暴卒，謚曰沖公。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, Tianshi had Su and others lead troops by night into the palace, assassinated Xuanjing, and proclaimed sudden death; his posthumous title was Duke Chong.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, Tianshi had Liu Su and others lead troops into the palace by night, assassinated Xuanjing, and announced that he had died suddenly. His posthumous title was Duke Chong.

sentences.zh: 天錫自稱使持節、大都督、大將軍、涼州牧、西平公，時年十八。

translations.literal: Tianshi styled himself Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Grand Commander, Grand General, Governor of Liang Province, and Duke of Xiping; he was then eighteen years old.
translations.idiomatic: Tianshi styled himself Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Grand Commander, Grand General, Governor of Liang Province, and Duke of Xiping. He was then eighteen years old.

sentences.zh: 尊母劉美人曰太妃。

translations.literal: He honored his mother Lady Liu as Grand Consort.
translations.idiomatic: He honored his mother Lady Liu as Grand Consort.

sentences.zh: 遣司馬綸騫奉章詣建康請命，並送御史俞歸東還。

translations.literal: He sent the Marshal Lun Qian to present a memorial at Jiankang to request imperial confirmation, and also sent back the Censor Yu Gui to the east.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Marshal Lun Qian to Jiankang with a memorial requesting imperial confirmation, and also sent Censor Yu Gui back east.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，大赦。

translations.literal: On guihai day a general amnesty was granted.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai day a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，燕鎮南將軍慕容塵攻陳留太守袁披於長平；

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Murong Chen, Pacifying-South General of Yan, attacked Yuan Pi, Administrator of Chenliu, at Changping;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, Yan's Pacifying-South General Murong Chen attacked Yuan Pi, Administrator of Chenliu, at Changping;

sentences.zh: 汝南太守朱斌乘虛襲許昌，克之。

translations.literal: Zhu Bin, Administrator of Runan, took advantage of the opening to strike Xuchang and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Bin, Administrator of Runan, took advantage of the opening to strike Xuchang and captured it.

sentences.zh: 代王什冀犍擊高車，大破之，俘獲萬餘口，馬、牛、羊百餘萬頭。

translations.literal: The Dai king Shiyijian attacked the Gaoche, routed them utterly, captured more than ten thousand persons, and took more than a million horses, cattle, and sheep.
translations.idiomatic: The Dai king Shiyijian attacked the Gaoche and routed them utterly, capturing more than ten thousand people and more than a million horses, cattle, and sheep.

sentences.zh: 以征虜將軍桓沖為江州刺史。

translations.literal: Campaign-Against-Barbarians General Huan Chong was made Inspector of Jiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Campaign-Against-Barbarians General Huan Chong was appointed Inspector of Jiang Province.

sentences.zh: 十一月，姚襄故將張駿殺江州督護趙毘，帥其徒北叛；

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Zhang Jun, a former officer of Yao Xiang, killed Zhao Pi, Military Administrator of Jiang Province, and led his followers in rebellion to the north;
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Zhang Jun, a former officer of Yao Xiang, killed Zhao Pi, Military Administrator of Jiang Province, and led his followers in rebellion northward;

sentences.zh: 沖討斬之。

translations.literal: Chong pursued and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Chong pursued and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 孝宗穆皇帝下興寧二年（

translations.literal: The second year of Xingning under Emperor Xiaozong Mu (
translations.idiomatic: Second year of Xingning, reign of Emperor Xiaozong Mu (

sentences.zh: 甲子，公元三六四年）

translations.literal: jiazi, AD 364)
translations.idiomatic: jiazi year, AD 364)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丙辰，燕大赦。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on bingchen day, Yan granted a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on bingchen day, Yan proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 二月，燕太傅評、龍驤將軍李洪略地河南。

translations.literal: In the second month, the Grand Tutor Ping and Flying-Dragon General Li Hong of Yan raided territory in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Yan's Grand Tutor Murong Ping and Flying-Dragon General Li Hong raided territory south of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 三月，庚戌朔，大閱戶口，令所在土斷，嚴其法制，謂之《庚戌制》。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the first day gengxu, a great census of households was conducted; orders were issued for local registration by native land, with strict legal enforcement—it was called the "Gengxu Regulations."
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the first day gengxu, a great census of households was conducted and orders were issued for local registration by native land under strict enforcement. It was called the Gengxu Regulations.

sentences.zh: 帝信方士言，斷谷餌藥以求長生。

translations.literal: The Emperor believed the words of magicians, cut off grain and took elixirs seeking long life.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor believed the words of magicians, abstained from grain, and took elixirs in pursuit of long life.

sentences.zh: 侍中高崧諫曰：「此非成乘所宜為；

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Gao Song remonstrated: "This is not what one who rides the completed chariot should do;
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Gao Song remonstrated: "This is not what one who sits in the completed chariot should do;

sentences.zh: 陛下茲事，實日月之食。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's pursuing this matter is truly an eclipse of sun and moon.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's pursuit of this is truly an eclipse of sun and moon.

sentences.zh: 」不聽。

translations.literal: " He did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor did not listen.

sentences.zh: 辛未，帝以藥發，不能親萬機，褚太后復臨朝攝政。

translations.literal: On xinwei day the Emperor, because the elixir took effect, could not personally handle the myriad affairs; Empress Dowager Chu again attended court and held regency.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei day the elixir took effect and the Emperor could not personally attend to affairs. Empress Dowager Chu again attended court as regent.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，甲辰，燕李洪攻許昌、汝南，敗晉兵於懸瓠，穎川太守李福戰死，汝南太守朱斌奔壽春，陳郡太守朱輔退保彭城。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on jiachen day, Li Hong of Yan attacked Xuchang and Runan, defeated Jin forces at Xuanhuo; Li Fu, Administrator of Yingchuan, died in battle; Zhu Bin, Administrator of Runan, fled to Shouchun; Zhu Fu, Administrator of Chen commandery, withdrew to hold Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on jiachen day, Li Hong of Yan attacked Xuchang and Runan and defeated Jin forces at Xuanhuo. Li Fu, Administrator of Yingchuan, died in battle; Zhu Bin, Administrator of Runan, fled to Shouchun; and Zhu Fu, Administrator of Chen, withdrew to hold Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 大司馬溫遣西中郎將袁真等御之，溫帥舟師屯合肥。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Wen sent Western Central General Yuan Zhen and others to resist them; Wen led river forces and encamped at Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Huan Wen sent Western Central General Yuan Zhen and others to resist them and led river forces to encamp at Hefei.

sentences.zh: 燕人遂拔許昌、汝南、陳郡，徙萬餘戶於幽、冀二州，遣鎮南將軍慕容塵屯許昌。

translations.literal: The Yan forces then took Xuchang, Runan, and Chen commandery, moved more than ten thousand households to You and Ji provinces, and sent Pacifying-South General Murong Chen to encamp at Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan forces then took Xuchang, Runan, and Chen commandery, relocated more than ten thousand households to You and Ji provinces, and sent Pacifying-South General Murong Chen to encamp at Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 五月，戊辰，以揚州刺史王述為尚書令。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on wuchen day, Wang Shu, Inspector of Yang Province, was made Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on wuchen day, Wang Shu, Inspector of Yang Province, was appointed Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 加大司馬溫揚州牧、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Wen was further made Governor of Yang Province and Recorder of the Masters of Writing Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Huan Wen was further appointed Governor of Yang Province and Recorder of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 壬申，使侍中召溫入參朝政，溫辭不至。

translations.literal: On renshen day a Palace Attendant was sent to summon Wen to join in court governance; Wen declined and did not come.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen day an edict sent a Palace Attendant to summon Huan Wen to join in court governance. Huan Wen declined and did not come.

sentences.zh: 王述每受職，不為虛讓，其所辭必於不受。

translations.literal: Whenever Wang Shu received an appointment he did not make empty declinations; when he declined it was because he would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Wang Shu received an appointment he never made empty declinations; when he declined, it was because he would not accept.

sentences.zh: 及為尚書令，子坦之白述：「故事當讓。

translations.literal: When he became Director of the Masters of Writing, his son Tanzhi told Shu: "By precedent one should decline.
translations.idiomatic: When he became Director of the Masters of Writing, his son Tanzhi told Wang Shu, "By precedent one should decline.

sentences.zh: 」述曰：「汝謂我不堪邪？

translations.literal: " Shu said, "Do you think I am not up to it?
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Shu said, "Do you think I am not up to it?

sentences.zh: 」坦之曰：「非也，但克讓自美事耳！

translations.literal: " Tanzhi said, "Not so—only that restrained declination is itself a fine thing!
translations.idiomatic: " Tanzhi said, "Not at all. Restrained declination is simply a fine thing in itself!

sentences.zh: 」述曰：「既謂堪之，何為復讓！

translations.literal: " Shu said, "Since you say I am up to it, why decline again!
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Shu said, "Since you say I am up to it, why should I decline again!

sentences.zh: 人言汝勝我，定不及也。

translations.literal: People say you surpass me—you surely fall short of it.
translations.idiomatic: People say you surpass me—you surely fall short of that.

sentences.zh: 六月，秦王堅遣大鴻臚拜張天錫為大將軍、涼州牧、西平公。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, King Fu Jian of Qin sent the Grand Herald to invest Zhang Tianshi as Grand General, Governor of Liang Province, and Duke of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, King Fu Jian of Qin sent the Grand Herald to invest Zhang Tianshi as Grand General, Governor of Liang Province, and Duke of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，丁卯，詔復徵大司馬溫入朝。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on dingmao day, an edict again summoned Grand Marshal Wen to court.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on dingmao day, an edict again summoned Grand Marshal Huan Wen to court.

sentences.zh: 八月，溫至赭圻，詔尚書車灌止之，溫遂城赭圻居之，固讓內錄，遙領揚州牧。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Wen reached Zheqi; an edict from the Masters of Writing with Che Guan ordered him to stop; Wen then fortified Zheqi and dwelt there, firmly declining the inner recorder post and holding the governorship of Yang Province at a distance.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Huan Wen reached Zheqi. An edict from the Masters of Writing with Che Guan ordered him to stop. Huan Wen then fortified Zheqi and took up residence there, firmly declining the inner recorder post while holding the governorship of Yang Province at a distance.

sentences.zh: 秦汝南公騰謀反，伏誅。

translations.literal: Teng, Duke of Runan of Qin, plotted rebellion and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Teng, Duke of Runan of Qin, plotted rebellion and was executed.

sentences.zh: 騰，秦主生之弟也。

translations.literal: Teng was the younger brother of the Qin ruler Fu Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Teng was the younger brother of the Qin ruler Fu Sheng.

sentences.zh: 是時，生弟晉公柳等猶有五人，王猛言於堅曰：「不去五公，終必為患。

translations.literal: At this time Fu Sheng's younger brothers, including Duke of Jin Liu and others, still numbered five in all. Wang Meng said to Fu Jian: "If the Five Dukes are not removed, in the end they will surely become a peril.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Fu Sheng's younger brothers, including Duke of Jin Liu and others, still numbered five in all. Wang Meng said to Fu Jian, "If the Five Dukes are not removed, they will become a peril in the end.

sentences.zh: 」堅不從。

translations.literal: " Fu Jian did not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: " Fu Jian did not heed him.

sentences.zh: 燕侍中慕龍輿詣龍城，徙宗廟及所留百官皆詣鄴。

translations.literal: Yan's Attendant-in-Ordinary Murong Longyu went to Longcheng; the relocated ancestral temples and all officials left behind all went to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Longyu, Attendant-in-Ordinary of Yan, went to Longcheng, and the moved ancestral temples and every official who had remained behind all proceeded to Ye.

sentences.zh: 燕太宰恪將取洛陽，先遣人招納士民，遠近諸塢皆歸之；

translations.literal: Yan's Grand Preceptor Ke was about to take Luoyang. He first sent men to win over gentry and commoners, and walled forts near and far all submitted to him;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Murong Ke of Yan prepared to take Luoyang. He first sent men to win over local gentry and commoners, and fortified settlements near and far all submitted to him;

sentences.zh: 乃使司馬悅希軍於盟津，豫州刺史孫興軍於成皋。

translations.literal: He then stationed Marshal Yue Xi at Mengjin and Inspector of Yu Sun Xing at Chenggao.
translations.idiomatic: He then stationed Marshal Yue Xi at Mengjin and Inspector of Yu Sun Xing at Chenggao.

sentences.zh: 初，沈充之子勁，以其父死於逆亂，志欲立功以雪舊恥；

translations.literal: At first, Shen Chong's son Jin, because his father had died in rebellion and disorder, resolved to achieve merit and wipe away the old shame;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Shen Jin, son of Shen Chong, because his father had died in rebellion and disorder, resolved to win merit and wipe away the old shame;

sentences.zh: 年三十餘，以刑家不得仕。

translations.literal: He was over thirty years of age, but as one from a punished family he could not hold office.
translations.idiomatic: He was over thirty, but as the son of a criminal house he was barred from office.

sentences.zh: 吳興太守王胡之為司州刺史，上疏稱勁才行，請解禁錮，參其府事，朝廷許之。

translations.literal: Wang Huzhi, governor of Wuxing, was appointed Inspector of Si and memorialized praising Jin's ability and conduct, requesting that the ban on office be lifted so he might serve on the inspector's staff; the court granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huzhi, governor of Wuxing, was appointed Inspector of Si. He memorialized praising Jin's talent and conduct and asked that the ban on office be lifted so Jin might serve on his staff; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 會胡之以病，不行。

translations.literal: Just then Huzhi fell ill and did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: But Huzhi fell ill and never took up the post.

sentences.zh: 及燕人逼洛陽，冠軍將軍陳祐守之，眾不過二千。

translations.literal: When the Yan forces pressed Luoyang, Champion General Chen You held it with no more than two thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan forces pressed Luoyang, Champion General Chen You held the city with fewer than two thousand men.

sentences.zh: 勁自表求配祐效力；

translations.literal: Jin petitioned on his own account asking to be assigned to Chen You to serve;
translations.idiomatic: Jin petitioned on his own account, asking to be assigned to Chen You's command;

sentences.zh: 詔以勁補冠軍長史，令自募壯士，得千餘人以行。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Jin Champion Chief Clerk, ordered him to recruit stout fighting men himself, and he gathered a thousand-odd men and set out.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Jin Champion Chief Clerk and ordered him to recruit fighting men on his own. He raised more than a thousand men and marched.

sentences.zh: 勁屢以少擊燕眾，摧破之。

translations.literal: Jin repeatedly struck Yan's larger forces with smaller numbers and smashed them.
translations.idiomatic: Jin repeatedly attacked Yan's larger forces with smaller numbers and broke them.

sentences.zh: 而洛陽糧盡援絕，祐自度不能守，乃以救許昌為名，九月，留勁以五百人守洛陽，祐帥眾而東。

translations.literal: But Luoyang's grain was exhausted and reinforcements cut off. You judged for himself that he could not hold the city, so under the pretext of rescuing Xuchang, in the ninth month he left Jin with five hundred men to hold Luoyang and led the main force east.
translations.idiomatic: But Luoyang's grain was gone and relief cut off. You judged that he could not hold the city, so under the pretext of rescuing Xuchang, in the ninth month he left Jin with five hundred men to defend Luoyang and led the main force east.

sentences.zh: 勁喜曰：「吾志欲致命，今得之矣。

translations.literal: Jin said with joy: "My ambition has been to give my life—I have my wish at last.
translations.idiomatic: Jin said joyfully, "My ambition has been to give my life—and now I have my chance.

sentences.zh: 」祐聞許昌已沒，遂奔新城。

translations.literal: " When You heard that Xuchang had already fallen, he fled to Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: " When You heard that Xuchang had already fallen, he fled to Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 燕悅希引兵略河南諸城，盡取之。

translations.literal: Yan's Yue Xi led troops to overrun the cities of Henan and took them all.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Xi of Yan led troops to overrun the cities of Henan and took them all.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅命公國各置三卿，並餘官皆聽自采辟，獨為置郎中令。

translations.literal: King of Qin Fu Jian ordered that each princely state establish three chief ministers, and that all other offices might be filled by their own recruitment—only the Palace Master was to be appointed by him.
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian of Qin ordered each princely state to establish three chief ministers and allowed all other offices to be filled by their own recruitment; only the Palace Master he would appoint himself.

sentences.zh: 富商趙掇等車服僭侈，諸公競引以為卿。

translations.literal: Rich merchants such as Zhao Duo had carriages and apparel in usurping extravagance, and the princes vied to bring them in as chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy merchants such as Zhao Duo rode in carriages and wore robes of usurping extravagance, and the princes vied to appoint them chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 黃門侍郎安定程憲言於堅，請治之。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant of the Yellow Gate Cheng Xian of Anding spoke to Fu Jian and asked that this be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Cheng Xian of Anding spoke to Fu Jian and asked that the matter be punished.

sentences.zh: 堅乃下詔稱：「本欲使諸公延選英儒，乃更猥濫如是！

translations.literal: Fu Jian then issued an edict saying: "I intended that the princes should seek out and select worthy scholars—yet it has become so coarse and indiscriminate!
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian then issued an edict saying, "I meant for the princes to seek out worthy scholars—yet the appointments have become so coarse and indiscriminate!

sentences.zh: 宜令有司推檢，辟召非其人者，悉降爵為侯，自今國官皆委之銓衡。

translations.literal: The responsible offices should investigate: all who were recruited or summoned though unfit for office shall be demoted in rank to marquis; from now on state offices shall all be entrusted to the board of evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: Let the responsible offices investigate. All who were recruited though unfit for office shall be demoted to marquis. From now on, state offices shall all be entrusted to the board of evaluation.

sentences.zh: 自非命士已上，不得乘車馬；

translations.literal: None below the rank of appointed scholar might ride horses or carriages;
translations.idiomatic: None below the rank of appointed scholar might ride horses or carriages;

sentences.zh: 去京師百里內，工商皁隸，不得服金銀、錦繡。

translations.literal: Within a hundred li of the capital, merchants, artisans, and common servants might not wear gold, silver, brocade, or embroidery.
translations.idiomatic: Within a hundred li of the capital, merchants, artisans, and common servants might not wear gold, silver, brocade, or embroidery.

sentences.zh: 犯者棄市！

translations.literal: Violators were executed in the marketplace!
translations.idiomatic: Violators were executed in the marketplace!

sentences.zh: 」於是平陽、平昌、九江、陳留、安樂五公皆降爵為侯。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the five princes of Pingyang, Pingchang, Jiujiang, Chenliu, and Anle were all demoted to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon the five princes of Pingyang, Pingchang, Jiujiang, Chenliu, and Anle were all demoted to marquis.

translations.idiomatic: Third year of Xingning, reign of Emperor Xiaozong Mu (

translations.idiomatic: yichou year, AD 365)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，庚申，皇后王氏崩。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on gengshen day, Empress Wang died.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on gengshen day, Empress Wang died.

sentences.zh: 劉衛辰復叛代，代王什翼犍東渡河，擊走之。

translations.literal: Liu Weichen again rebelled against Dai. The Dai king Tuoba Shiyijian crossed the Yellow River eastward and struck him, driving him off.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Weichen again rebelled against Dai. The Dai king Tuoba Shiyijian crossed the Yellow River eastward, attacked him, and drove him off.

sentences.zh: 什翼犍性寬厚，郎中令許謙盜絹二匹，什翼犍知而匿之，謂左長史燕鳳曰：「吾不忍視謙之面，卿慎勿洩。

translations.literal: Shiyijian was by nature generous and mild. Palace Master Xu Qian stole two bolts of silk. Shiyijian knew but concealed it, and said to Left Chief Clerk Yan Feng: "I cannot bear to look Qian in the face—you must take care not to reveal this.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyijian was by nature generous and mild. Palace Master Xu Qian stole two bolts of silk. Shiyijian knew but concealed it and said to Left Chief Clerk Yan Feng, "I cannot bear to look Qian in the face. You must take care not to reveal this.

sentences.zh: 若謙慚而自殺，是吾以財殺士也。

translations.literal: If Qian, in shame, should kill himself, I would have killed a worthy man for the sake of property.
translations.idiomatic: If Qian, in shame, should kill himself, I would have killed a worthy man for the sake of property.

sentences.zh: 」嘗討西部叛者，流矢中目；

translations.literal: afterwards, when the archer was captured, the ministers wished to dismember him slice by slice. Shiyijian said: "Each man fought for his own lord—what crime is this!
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the archer was captured, the ministers wished to dismember him. Shiyijian said, "Each man fought for his own lord—what crime is that!

sentences.zh: 」遂釋之。

translations.literal: " So he released him.
translations.idiomatic: " So he released him.

sentences.zh: 大司馬溫移鎮姑孰。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Huan Wen moved his headquarters to Gushu.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Huan Wen moved his headquarters to Gushu.

sentences.zh: 二月，乙未，以其弟右將軍豁監荊州、揚州之義城、雍州之京兆諸軍事，領荊州刺史，加江州刺史桓沖監江州及荊、豫八郡諸軍事，並假節。

translations.literal: In the second month, on yiwei day, his younger brother Right General Huan Huo was made overseer of military affairs for Yicheng in Jing and Yang and Jingzhao in Yong, with concurrent appointment as Inspector of Jing; Inspector of Jiang Huan Chong was additionally made overseer of military affairs for Jiang and eight commanderies of Jing and Yu—both with the credential of staff.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on yiwei day, his younger brother Right General Huan Huo was made overseer of military affairs for Yicheng in Jing and Yang and Jingzhao in Yong, with concurrent appointment as Inspector of Jing. Inspector of Jiang Huan Chong was additionally made overseer of military affairs for Jiang and eight commanderies of Jing and Yu; both received the credential of staff.

sentences.zh: 司徒昱聞陳祐棄洛陽，會大司馬溫於洌洲，共議征討。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Yu, hearing that Chen You had abandoned Luoyang, met Grand Marshal Huan Wen at Liezhou to discuss a punitive campaign together.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Yu, hearing that Chen You had abandoned Luoyang, met Grand Marshal Huan Wen at Liezhou to discuss a punitive campaign.

sentences.zh: 丙申，帝崩於西堂，事遂寢。

translations.literal: On bingshen day the Emperor died in the Western Hall, and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen day the emperor died in the Western Hall, and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 帝無嗣，丁酉，皇太后詔以琅邪王奕承大統。

translations.literal: The Emperor had no heir. On dingyou day the Empress Dowager issued an edict that Prince of Langye Yi should succeed to the Great Succession.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had no heir. On dingyou day the empress dowager issued an edict that Prince of Langye Yi should succeed to the throne.

sentences.zh: 百官奉迎於琅邪第，是日，即皇帝位，大赦。

translations.literal: The officials welcomed him at the Langye residence. That same day he took the imperial throne and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: The officials welcomed him at the Langye residence. That same day he took the throne and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 秦大赦，改元建元。

translations.literal: Qin proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Jianyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Qin proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Jianyuan.

sentences.zh: 燕太宰恪、吳王垂共攻洛陽。

translations.literal: Yan's Grand Preceptor Ke and Prince of Wu Chui jointly attacked Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Murong Ke and Murong Chui, Prince of Wu, jointly attacked Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 恪謂諸將曰：「卿等常患吾不攻，今洛陽城高而兵弱，易克也，勿更畏懦而怠惰！

translations.literal: Ke said to the generals: "You have often worried that I would not attack. Now Luoyang's walls are high but its troops few—it is easy to take. Do not grow fearful and slack again!
translations.idiomatic: Ke said to the generals, "You have often complained that I would not attack. Now Luoyang's walls are high but its troops few—it is easy to take. Do not grow fearful and slack again!

sentences.zh: 」遂攻之。

translations.literal: " Then he attacked it.
translations.idiomatic: " Then he attacked it.

sentences.zh: 三月，克之，執揚武將軍沈勁。

translations.literal: In the third month they took it and seized Yangwu General Shen Jin.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month they took the city and captured Yangwu General Shen Jin.

sentences.zh: 勁神氣自若，恪將宥之。

translations.literal: Jin's spirit and bearing were unperturbed. Ke was about to spare him.
translations.idiomatic: Jin remained calm in spirit and bearing. Ke was about to spare him.

sentences.zh: 中軍將軍慕輿虔曰：「勁雖奇士，觀其志度，終不為人用，今赦之，必為後患。

translations.literal: Central Army General Muyu Qian said: "Though Jin is a remarkable man, judging his resolve and bearing, in the end he will never serve another's use. If you pardon him now, he will surely become a future peril.
translations.idiomatic: Central Army General Muyu Qian said, "Though Jin is a remarkable man, judging his resolve and bearing, in the end he will never serve another. If you pardon him now, he will surely become a future peril.

sentences.zh: 」遂殺之。

translations.literal: " So they killed him.
translations.idiomatic: " So they killed him.

sentences.zh: 恪略地至崤、澠，關中大震，秦王堅自將屯陝城以備之。

translations.literal: Ke overran territory as far as Xiao and Mian. Guanzhong was greatly shaken. King of Qin Fu Jian personally led troops and encamped at Shancheng to guard against him.
translations.idiomatic: Ke overran territory as far as Xiao and Mian. Guanzhong was greatly shaken. King Fu Jian of Qin personally led troops and encamped at Shancheng to guard against him.

sentences.zh: 燕人以左中郎將慕容築為洛州刺史，鎮金墉；

translations.literal: The Yan people made Left Court Gentleman Murong Zhu governor of Luo, stationed at Jin Yong;
translations.idiomatic: The Yan court made Left Court Gentleman Murong Zhu governor of Luo, stationed at Jin Yong;

sentences.zh: 吳王垂為都督荊、揚、洛、徐、兗、豫、雍、益、涼、秦十州諸軍事、征南大將軍、荊州牧，配方一萬，鎮魯陽。

translations.literal: Prince of Wu Chui was made overseer of military affairs for the ten provinces of Jing, Yang, Luo, Xu, Yan, Yu, Yong, Yi, Liang, and Qin, General Who Conquers the South, and governor of Jing, with a complement of ten thousand, stationed at Luyang.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui, Prince of Wu, was made overseer of military affairs for the ten provinces of Jing, Yang, Luo, Xu, Yan, Yu, Yong, Yi, Liang, and Qin, General Who Conquers the South, and governor of Jing, with a complement of ten thousand men, stationed at Luyang.

sentences.zh: 太宰恪還鄴，謂僚屬曰：「吾前平廣固，不能濟辟閭蔚；

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor Ke returned to Ye and said to his staff: "When I earlier pacified Guanggu, I could not save Bilu Wei;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Ke returned to Ye and said to his staff, "When I earlier pacified Guanggu, I could not save Bilu Wei;

sentences.zh: 今定洛陽，使沈勁為戮；

translations.literal: now, having secured Luoyang, I allowed Shen Jin to be slain;
translations.idiomatic: now, having secured Luoyang, I allowed Shen Jin to be slain;

sentences.zh: 雖皆非本情，然身為元帥，實有愧於四海。

translations.literal: though neither was my true intent, yet as commander I am truly shamed before all the realm.
translations.idiomatic: though neither was my true intent, yet as commander I am truly shamed before all the realm.

sentences.zh: 」朝廷嘉勁之忠，贈東陽太守。

translations.literal: " The court praised Jin's loyalty and posthumously honored him as Governor of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: " The court praised Jin's loyalty and posthumously honored him as Governor of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：沈勁可謂能子矣！

translations.literal: Your servant Guang says: Shen Jin may be called a capable son indeed!
translations.idiomatic: Your servant Guang says: Shen Jin may truly be called a capable son!

sentences.zh: 恥父之惡，致死以滌之，變凶逆之族為忠義之門。

translations.literal: Ashamed of his father's evil, he gave his life to wash it away, transforming a rebellious and traitorous clan into a household of loyalty and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed of his father's evil, he gave his life to wash it away, transforming a rebellious and traitorous clan into a household of loyalty and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：「干父之蠱，用譽。

translations.literal: The Book of Changes says: "He rectifies his father's corruption, and winning fame thereby.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says, "He rectifies his father's corruption, and winning fame thereby.

sentences.zh: 」《蔡仲之命》曰：「爾尚蓋前人之愆，惟忠惟孝。

translations.literal: " The Charge to Cai Zhong says: "You still cover your forebears' faults—being loyal, being filial.
translations.idiomatic: " The Charge to Cai Zhong says, "You still cover your forebears' faults—being loyal, being filial.

sentences.zh: 」其是之謂乎！

translations.literal: " Is this not what those lines mean!
translations.idiomatic: " Is this not what those lines mean!

sentences.zh: 太宰恪為將，不事威嚴，專用恩信，撫士卒務綜大要，不為苛令，使人人得便安。

translations.literal: As a commander, Grand Preceptor Ke did not rely on stern authority but used kindness and trust alone. In comforting his troops he attended to the broad essentials, issuing no harsh orders, so that every man could find ease and security.
translations.idiomatic: As a commander, Grand Preceptor Ke did not rely on stern authority but used kindness and trust alone. In comforting his troops he attended to the broad essentials, issuing no harsh orders, so that every man could find ease and security.

sentences.zh: 平時營中寬縱，似若可犯；

translations.literal: In normal times the camp was relaxed and indulgent, as though it might be violated;
translations.idiomatic: In normal times the camp was relaxed and indulgent, as though it might be violated;

sentences.zh: 然警備嚴密，敵至莫能近者，故未嘗負敗。

translations.literal: yet its watch and defenses were strict, and when enemies came none could approach—therefore he never suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: yet its watch and defenses were strict, and when enemies came none could approach. Therefore he never suffered defeat.

sentences.zh: 壬申，葬哀帝及靜皇后於安平陵。

translations.literal: On renshen day, Emperor Ai and Empress Jing were buried at Anping Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen day, Emperor Ai and Empress Jing were buried at Anping Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，壬午，燕太尉武平匡公封弈卒。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on renwu day, Yan's Grand Commandant, Duke of Wuping and Kang, Feng Yi, died.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on renwu day, Feng Yi, Grand Commandant of Yan and Duke of Wuping and Kang, died.

sentences.zh: 以司空陽鶩為太尉，侍中、光祿大夫皇甫真為司空，領中書監。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Yang Xu was made Grand Commandant; Palace Attendant and Household Grandee Huangfu Zhen was made Minister of Works, with concurrent appointment as Overseer of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Yang Xu was made Grand Commandant; Palace Attendant and Household Grandee Huangfu Zhen was made Minister of Works, with concurrent appointment as Overseer of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 騖歷事四朝，年耆望重，自太宰恪以下皆拜之。

translations.literal: Xu had served through four reigns; old in years and heavy in repute, all from Grand Preceptor Ke downward bowed to him.
translations.idiomatic: Xu had served through four reigns. Old in years and heavy in repute, all from Grand Preceptor Ke downward bowed to him.

sentences.zh: 而騖謙恭謹厚，過於少時；

translations.literal: Yet Xu was more humble, deferential, careful, and earnest than in his youth;
translations.idiomatic: Yet Xu was more humble, deferential, careful, and earnest than in his youth;

sentences.zh: 戒束子孫，雖朱紫羅列，無敢違犯其法度者。

translations.literal: he admonished and restrained his descendants, and though official ranks of red and purple stood in rows, none dared violate his standards.
translations.idiomatic: he admonished and restrained his descendants, and though official ranks of red and purple stood in rows, none dared violate his standards.

sentences.zh: 六月，戊子，益州刺史建城襄會周撫卒。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on wuzi day, Inspector of Yi, Duke of Jiancheng and Xiang, Zhou Fu, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on wuzi day, Zhou Fu, Inspector of Yi and Duke of Jiancheng and Xiang, died.

sentences.zh: 撫在益州三十餘年，甚有威惠。

translations.literal: Fu had been in Yi Province for more than thirty years and possessed great prestige and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Fu had governed Yi Province for more than thirty years and possessed great prestige and kindness.

sentences.zh: 詔以其子犍為太守楚代之。

translations.literal: An edict appointed his son Jian governor in place of Chu to succeed him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed his son Jian governor to succeed Zhou Chu.
