translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on jiyou day, Prince of Guiji Yu was restored to Prince of Langye.

sentences.zh: 壬子，立妃庾氏為皇后。

translations.literal: On renzi day, Lady Yu was established as Empress.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi day, Lady Yu was established as empress.

sentences.zh: -{后}-，冰之女也。

translations.literal: The empress was the daughter of Bing.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was the daughter of Yu Bing.

sentences.zh: 甲申，立琅邪王昱子昌明為會稽王；

translations.literal: On jiashen day, Langye Prince Yu's son Changming was made Prince of Guiji;
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen day, Langye Prince Yu's son Changming was made Prince of Guiji;

sentences.zh: 昱固讓，猶自稱會稽王。

translations.literal: Yu steadfastly declined and still styled himself Prince of Guiji.
translations.idiomatic: Yu steadfastly declined and still styled himself Prince of Guiji.

sentences.zh: 匈奴右賢王曹轂、左賢王劉衛辰皆叛秦。

translations.literal: Cao Gu, Right Worthy King of the Xiongnu, and Liu Weichen, Left Worthy King, both rebelled against Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Gu, Right Worthy King of the Xiongnu, and Liu Weichen, Left Worthy King, both rebelled against Qin.

sentences.zh: 轂帥眾二萬寇杏城，秦王堅自將討之，使衛大將軍李威、左僕射王猛輔太子宏留守長安。

translations.literal: Gu led twenty thousand men to raid Xingcheng. King of Qin Fu Jian personally led troops to attack him, sending Guard General Li Wei and Left Deputy Director Wang Meng to assist Crown Prince Hong in holding Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Gu led twenty thousand men to raid Xingcheng. King Fu Jian of Qin personally led troops against him, sending Guard General Li Wei and Left Deputy Director Wang Meng to assist Crown Prince Hong in holding Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 八月，堅擊轂，破之，斬轂弟活，轂請降，徙其豪傑六千餘戶於安。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Fu Jian struck Gu, defeated him, beheaded Gu's younger brother Huo, Gu requested surrender, and more than six thousand leading families were moved to An.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Fu Jian struck Gu, defeated him, beheaded Gu's younger brother Huo, accepted Gu's surrender, and moved more than six thousand leading families to An.

sentences.zh: 建節將軍鄧羌討衛辰，擒之於木根山。

translations.literal: General Bearing the Staff Deng Qiang pursued Weichen and captured him at Mugen Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: General Bearing the Staff Deng Qiang pursued Weichen and captured him at Mugen Mountain.

sentences.zh: 九月，堅如朔方，巡撫諸胡。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Fu Jian went to Shuofang to tour and comfort the various Hu peoples.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Fu Jian went to Shuofang to tour and comfort the various Hu peoples.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，征北將軍、淮南公幼帥杏城之眾乘虛襲長安，李威擊斬之。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Campaign-North General and Duke of Huainan You led the Xingcheng host to seize an opening and raid Chang'an. Li Wei struck and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, Campaign-North General and Duke of Huainan Fu You led the Xingcheng host to seize an opening and raid Chang'an. Li Wei struck and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑禿髮椎斤卒，年一百一十，子思復鞬代統其眾。

translations.literal: The Xianbei chief Tufa Chuijin died at the age of one hundred and ten. His son Tufa Sirong succeeded him in commanding the tribe.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianbei chief Tufa Chuijin died at the age of one hundred and ten. His son Tufa Sirong succeeded him in commanding the tribe.

sentences.zh: 椎斤，樹機能從弟務丸之孫也。

translations.literal: Chuijin was the grandson of Wuwanyan, younger brother by a collateral line of Tufa Shuneng.
translations.idiomatic: Chuijin was the grandson of Wuwanyan, a collateral kinsman of Tufa Shuneng.

sentences.zh: 梁州刺史司馬勳，為政酷暴，治中、別駕及州之豪右，言語忤意，即於坐梟斬之，或親射殺之。

translations.literal: Sima Xun, Inspector of Liang, governed with cruel brutality. If chief clerks, aides, or leading families of the province spoke in ways that offended him, he would on the spot behead and expose their corpses, or personally shoot them dead.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xun, Inspector of Liang, governed with cruel brutality. If chief clerks, aides, or leading families of the province spoke in ways that offended him, he would on the spot behead and expose their corpses, or personally shoot them dead.

sentences.zh: 常有據蜀之志，憚周撫，不敢發。

translations.literal: He often harbored the ambition to hold Shu, but feared Zhou Fu and did not act.
translations.idiomatic: He often harbored the ambition to hold Shu, but feared Zhou Fu and did not act.

sentences.zh: 及撫卒，勳遂舉兵反。

translations.literal: When Fu died, Xun at once raised troops in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu died, Xun at once raised troops in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 別駕雍端、西戎司馬隗粹切諫，勳皆殺之，自號梁、益二州牧、成都王。

translations.literal: Aide Yong Duan and Western Rong Major Wei Cui urged him sharply; Xun killed them both and styled himself Governor of Liang and Yi and King of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Aide Yong Duan and Western Rong Major Wei Cui urged him sharply; Xun killed them both and styled himself Governor of Liang and Yi and King of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 十一月，勳引兵入劍閣，攻涪，西夷校尉毌丘暐棄城走。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Xun led troops through Jian'ge Pass, attacked Fu, and Commandant of Pacification for the Western Yi Muqiu Wei abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Xun led troops through Jian'ge Pass, attacked Fu, and Commandant of Pacification for the Western Yi Muqiu Wei abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，圍益州刺史周楚於成都。

translations.literal: On yimao day he besieged Inspector of Yi Zhou Chu in Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao day he besieged Inspector of Yi Zhou Chu in Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 大司馬溫表鷹揚將軍江夏相義陽朱序為征討都護以救之。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Huan Wen memorialized recommending Eagle-Hold General, Chancellor of Jiangxia, Zhu Xu of Yiyang as Supreme Commander for the punitive campaign to rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Huan Wen memorialized recommending Eagle-Hold General and Chancellor of Jiangxia Zhu Xu of Yiyang as supreme commander for the punitive campaign to rescue them.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅還長安，以李威守太尉，加侍中。

translations.literal: King of Qin Fu Jian returned to Chang'an and made Li Wei acting Grand Commandant, with additional appointment as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian of Qin returned to Chang'an and made Li Wei acting Grand Commandant, with additional appointment as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 以曹轂為雁門公，劉衛辰為夏陽公，各使統其部落。

translations.literal: Cao Gu was made Duke of Yanmen and Liu Weichen Duke of Xiayang, each charged to command his own tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Gu was made Duke of Yanmen and Liu Weichen Duke of Xiayang, each charged to command his own tribe.

sentences.zh: 十二月，戊戌，以尚書王彪之為僕射。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on wuxu day, Secretariat Director Wang Biaozhi was made Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on wuxu day, Secretariat Director Wang Biaozhi was made Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 孝宗穆皇帝下太和元年（

translations.literal: The first year of Taihe under Emperor Xiaozong Mu (
translations.idiomatic: First year of Taihe, reign of Emperor Xiaozong Mu (

sentences.zh: 丙寅，公元三六六年）

translations.literal: bingyin, AD 366)
translations.idiomatic: bingyin year, AD 366)

sentences.zh: 春，三月，荊州刺史桓豁使督護桓羆攻南鄭，討司馬勳。

translations.literal: In spring, the third month, Inspector of Jing Huan Huo sent Supervisor Huan Pi to attack Nanzheng and suppress Sima Xun.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the third month, Inspector of Jing Huan Huo sent Supervisor Huan Pi to attack Nanzheng and suppress Sima Xun.

sentences.zh: 燕太宰、大司馬恪，太傅、司徒評，稽首歸政，上章綬，請歸第；

translations.literal: Yan's Grand Preceptor and Grand Marshal Ke and Grand Tutor and Minister of Works Ping kowtowed and returned the government, presenting their seals and ribbons and requesting to retire to their mansions;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor and Grand Marshal Murong Ke and Grand Tutor and Minister of Works Murong Ping kowtowed and returned the government, presenting their seals and ribbons and requesting to retire to their mansions;

sentences.zh: 燕主□不許。

translations.literal: the Yan ruler did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Murong Wei did not consent.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，戊寅，皇后庾氏崩。

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, on wuyin day, Empress Yu died.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fifth month, on wuyin day, Empress Yu died.

sentences.zh: 朱序、周楚擊司馬勳，破之，擒勳及其黨，送大司馬溫；

translations.literal: Zhu Xu and Zhou Chu attacked Sima Xun, defeated him, captured Xun and his followers, and sent them to Grand Marshal Huan Wen;
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xu and Zhou Chu attacked Sima Xun, defeated him, captured Xun and his followers, and sent them to Grand Marshal Huan Wen;

sentences.zh: 溫皆斬之，傳首建康。

translations.literal: Wen beheaded them all and sent their heads to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen beheaded them all and sent their heads to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 代王什翼犍遣左長史燕鳳入貢於秦。

translations.literal: The Dai king Shiyijian sent Left Chief Clerk Yan Feng to present tribute to Qin.
translations.idiomatic: The Dai king Shiyijian sent Left Chief Clerk Yan Feng to present tribute to Qin.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，癸酉，葬孝皇后於敬平陵。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on guiyou day, the Empress Xiaomu was buried at Jingping Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on guiyou day, Empress Xiaomu was buried at Jingping Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 秦輔國將軍王猛、前將軍楊安、揚武將軍姚萇等帥眾二萬寇荊州，攻南鄉郡，荊州刺史桓豁救之；

translations.literal: Qin Assisting-the-State General Wang Meng, Vanguard General Yang An, Flourishing-Martial General Yao Chang, and others led twenty thousand troops to raid Jing Province, attacked Nanxiang Commandery, and Inspector of Jing Huan Huo came to rescue them;
translations.idiomatic: Qin Assisting-the-State General Wang Meng, Vanguard General Yang An, Flourishing-Martial General Yao Chang, and others led twenty thousand troops to raid Jing Province, attacked Nanxiang Commandery, and Inspector of Jing Huan Huo came to rescue them;

sentences.zh: 八月，軍於新野。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the army encamped at Xinye.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the army encamped at Xinye.

sentences.zh: 秦兵掠安陽民萬餘戶而還。

translations.literal: The Qin troops plundered more than ten thousand households of the people of Anyang and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Qin troops plundered more than ten thousand households in Anyang and returned.

sentences.zh: 九月，甲午，曲赦梁、益二州。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on jiawu day, a partial amnesty was proclaimed for Liang and Yi provinces.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on jiawu day, a partial amnesty was proclaimed for Liang and Yi provinces.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，加司徒昱丞相、錄尚書事，入朝不趨，贊拜不名，劍履上殿。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Minister of Works Yu was additionally made Chancellor and Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing; he did not hasten on entering court, was not called by name when assisting at an audience, and was permitted to enter the hall wearing sword and shoes.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, Minister of Works Yu was additionally made Chancellor and Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing; he did not hasten on entering court, was not called by name when assisting at an audience, and was permitted to enter the hall wearing sword and shoes.

sentences.zh: 張天錫遣使至秦境上，告絕於秦。

translations.literal: Zhang Tiansxi sent envoys to the Qin border to announce a break with Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tiansxi sent envoys to the Qin border to announce a break with Qin.

sentences.zh: 燕撫軍將軍下邳王厲寇兗州，拔魯、高平數郡，置守宰而還。

translations.literal: Yan Pacification-Army General, King of Xiapi Li, raided Yan Province, captured several commanderies including Lu and Gaoping, installed governors and wardens, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Pacification-Army General and King of Xiapi Murong Li raided Yan Province, captured several commanderies including Lu and Gaoping, installed governors and wardens, and returned.

sentences.zh: 初，隴西李儼以郡降秦，既而復通於張天錫。

translations.literal: Earlier, Li Yan of Longxi had surrendered his commandery to Qin, but afterward reopened contact with Zhang Tiansxi.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Li Yan of Longxi had surrendered his commandery to Qin, but afterward reopened contact with Zhang Tiansxi.

sentences.zh: 十二月，羌斂岐以略陽四千家叛秦，稱臣於儼；

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the Qiang chief Lianqi, with four thousand households of Lüeyang, rebelled against Qin and submitted to Yan as his subject;
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the Qiang chief Lianqi, with four thousand households of Lüeyang, rebelled against Qin and submitted to Li Yan as his subject;

sentences.zh: 儼於是拜置牧守，與秦、涼絕。

translations.literal: Yan then appointed regional governors and wardens, breaking with Qin and Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yan then appointed regional governors and wardens, breaking with Qin and Former Liang.

sentences.zh: 南陽督護趙億據宛城降燕，太守桓澹走保新野；

translations.literal: Supervisor of Nanyang Zhao Yi seized Wancheng and surrendered to Yan; Grand Administrator Huan Dan fled and held Xinye;
translations.idiomatic: Supervisor of Nanyang Zhao Yi seized Wancheng and surrendered to Yan; Grand Administrator Huan Dan fled and held Xinye;

sentences.zh: 燕人遣南中郎將趙盤自魯陽戌宛。

translations.literal: The Yan sent Palace Gentlemen-General Zhao Pan from Luyang to garrison Wan.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan sent Palace Gentlemen-General Zhao Pan from Luyang to garrison Wan.

sentences.zh: 徐、兗二州刺史庾希，以後族故，兄弟貴顯，大司馬溫忌之。

translations.literal: Inspector of Xu and Yan provinces Yu Xi, because of his connection to the empress's family, had brothers who were eminent and powerful; Grand Marshal Huan Wen resented this.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector of Xu and Yan provinces Yu Xi, because of his connection to the empress's family, had brothers who were eminent and powerful; Grand Marshal Huan Wen resented this.

sentences.zh: 孝宗穆皇帝下太和二年（

translations.literal: The second year of Taihe under Emperor Xiaozong Mu (
translations.idiomatic: Second year of Taihe, reign of Emperor Xiaozong Mu (

sentences.zh: 丁卯，公元三六七年）

translations.literal: dingmao, AD 367)
translations.idiomatic: dingmao year, AD 367)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，庾希坐不能救魯、高平，免官。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Yu Xi was dismissed from office for failing to rescue Lu and Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Yu Xi was dismissed from office for failing to rescue Lu and Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 二月，燕撫軍將軍下邳王厲、鎮北將軍宜都王桓襲敕勒。

translations.literal: In the second month, Yan Pacification-Army General King of Xiapi Li and North-Pacifying General King of Yidu Huan attacked the Tiele.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Yan Pacification-Army General and King of Xiapi Murong Li and North-Pacifying General and King of Yidu Murong Huan attacked the Tiele.

sentences.zh: 秦輔國將軍王猛、隴西太守姜衡、南安太守南安邵羌、揚武將軍姚萇等帥眾萬七千討斂岐。

translations.literal: Qin Assisting-the-State General Wang Meng, Governor of Longxi Jiang Heng, Governor of Nan'an Shao Qiang of Nan'an, Flourishing-Martial General Yao Chang, and others led seventeen thousand troops to suppress Lianqi.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Assisting-the-State General Wang Meng, Governor of Longxi Jiang Heng, Governor of Nan'an Shao Qiang, Flourishing-Martial General Yao Chang, and others led seventeen thousand troops to suppress Lianqi.

sentences.zh: 三月，張天錫遣前將軍楊遹向金城，征東將軍常據向左南，游擊將軍張統向白土，天錫自將三萬人屯倉松，以討李儼。

translations.literal: In the third month, Zhang Tiansxi sent Vanguard General Yang Yu toward Jincheng, East-Campaign General Chang Ju toward Zuonan, Mobile-Campaign General Zhang Tong toward Baitu, and Tiansxi personally led thirty thousand men to encamp at Cangsong to attack Li Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Zhang Tiansxi sent Vanguard General Yang Yu toward Jincheng, East-Campaign General Chang Ju toward Zuonan, Mobile-Campaign General Zhang Tong toward Baitu, and Tiansxi personally led thirty thousand men to encamp at Cangsong to attack Li Yan.

sentences.zh: 斂岐部落先屬姚弋仲，聞姚萇至，皆降；

translations.literal: Lianqi's tribes had formerly belonged to Yao Yizhong; when they heard Yao Chang had arrived, they all surrendered;
translations.idiomatic: Lianqi's tribes had formerly belonged to Yao Yizhong; when they heard Yao Chang had arrived, they all surrendered;

sentences.zh: 王猛遂猛攻略陽。

translations.literal: Wang Meng then pressed the attack fiercely and took Lüeyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng then pressed the attack fiercely and took Lüeyang.

sentences.zh: 斂岐奔白馬。

translations.literal: Lianqi fled to Baima.
translations.idiomatic: Lianqi fled to Baima.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅以萇為隴東太守。

translations.literal: King of Qin Fu Jian made Chang Governor of Longdong.
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian of Qin made Yao Chang Governor of Longdong.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，燕慕容塵寇竟陵，太守羅崇擊破之。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Murong Chen of Yan raided Jingling; Grand Administrator Luo Chong struck and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Murong Chen of Yan raided Jingling; Grand Administrator Luo Chong struck and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 張天錫攻李儼大夏、武始二郡，下之。

translations.literal: Zhang Tiansxi attacked Li Yan's Daxia and Wushi commanderies and took them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tiansxi attacked Li Yan's Daxia and Wushi commanderies and took them.

sentences.zh: 常據敗儼兵於葵谷，天錫進屯左南。

translations.literal: Chang Ju defeated Yan's troops at Kuiguu Valley; Tiansxi advanced and encamped at Zuonan.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Ju defeated Li Yan's troops at Kuiguu Valley; Tiansxi advanced and encamped at Zuonan.

sentences.zh: 儼懼，退守枹罕，遣其兄子純謝罪於秦，且請救。

translations.literal: Yan, in fear, withdrew to defend Fuhan, sent his elder brother's son Chun to confess guilt to Qin, and also requested rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yan, in fear, withdrew to defend Fuhan, sent his elder brother's son Li Chun to confess guilt to Qin, and also requested rescue.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅使前將軍楊安、建威將軍王撫帥騎二萬，會王猛以救儼。

translations.literal: King of Qin Fu Jian sent Vanguard General Yang An and Establishing-Power General Wang Fu leading twenty thousand cavalry to join Wang Meng in rescuing Yan.
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian of Qin sent Vanguard General Yang An and Establishing-Power General Wang Fu leading twenty thousand cavalry to join Wang Meng in rescuing Li Yan.

sentences.zh: 猛遣邵羌追斂岐，王撫守侯和，姜衡守白石，猛與楊安救枹罕。

translations.literal: Meng sent Shao Qiang to pursue Lianqi; Wang Fu held Houhe, Jiang Heng held Baishi, and Meng with Yang An rescued Fuhan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng sent Shao Qiang to pursue Lianqi; Wang Fu held Houhe, Jiang Heng held Baishi, and Meng with Yang An rescued Fuhan.

sentences.zh: 天錫遣楊遹逆戰於枹罕東，猛大破之，俘斬萬七千級，與天錫相持於城下。

translations.literal: Tiansxi sent Yang Yu to meet them in battle east of Fuhan; Meng utterly defeated him, capturing and killing seventeen thousand, and faced off with Tiansxi below the city walls.
translations.idiomatic: Tiansxi sent Yang Yu to meet them in battle east of Fuhan; Wang Meng utterly defeated him, capturing and killing seventeen thousand, and faced off with Tiansxi below the city walls.

sentences.zh: 邵羌禽斂岐於白馬，送之。

translations.literal: Shao Qiang captured Lianqi at Baima and sent him in.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Qiang captured Lianqi at Baima and sent him in.

sentences.zh: 猛遺天錫書曰：「吾受詔救儼，不令與京州戰，今當深壁高壘，以聽後詔。

translations.literal: Meng sent Tiansxi a letter saying: "I have received orders to rescue Yan and was not commanded to fight Liang Province. For now I shall deepen the walls and raise high ramparts, awaiting further edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng sent Tiansxi a letter saying: "I have received orders to rescue Li Yan and was not commanded to fight Former Liang. For now I shall deepen the walls and raise high ramparts, awaiting further edicts.

sentences.zh: 曠曰持久，恐二家俱弊，非良算也。

translations.literal: A protracted stalemate, I fear, will wear both sides down—a poor strategy.
translations.idiomatic: A protracted stalemate, I fear, will wear both sides down—a poor strategy.

sentences.zh: 若將軍退捨，吾執儼而東，將軍徙民西旋，不亦可乎！

translations.literal: If you, General, withdraw, I shall take Yan in custody and move east, while you migrate your people westward—would that not also be acceptable!
translations.idiomatic: If you, General, withdraw, I shall take Li Yan in custody and move east, while you migrate your people westward—would that not also be acceptable!

sentences.zh: 」天錫謂諸將曰：「猛書如此；

translations.literal: Tiansxi said to his generals: "Meng's letter reads thus;
translations.idiomatic: Tiansxi said to his generals: "Wang Meng's letter reads thus;

sentences.zh: 吾本來伐叛，不來與秦戰。

translations.literal: I came originally to suppress rebellion, not to fight Qin.
translations.idiomatic: I came originally to suppress rebellion, not to fight Qin.

sentences.zh: 」遂引兵歸。

translations.literal: Then he led his troops back.
translations.idiomatic: Then he led his troops back.

sentences.zh: 李儼猶未納秦師，王猛白服乘輿，從者數十人，請與儼相見。

translations.literal: Li Yan had still not admitted the Qin army. Wang Meng, in white garments, rode in a carriage with only a few dozen attendants and requested to meet Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yan had still not admitted the Qin army. Wang Meng, in white garments, rode in a carriage with only a few dozen attendants and requested to meet Li Yan.

sentences.zh: 儼開門延之，未及為備，將士繼入，遂執儼。

translations.literal: Yan opened the gate and received him; before he could prepare defenses, soldiers followed in one after another, and they seized Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yan opened the gate and received him; before he could prepare defenses, soldiers followed in one after another, and they seized Li Yan.

sentences.zh: 以立忠將軍彭越為平西將軍、涼州刺史，鎮枹罕。

translations.literal: They made Establishing-Loyalty General Peng Yue Pacifying-West General and Inspector of Liang, stationed at Fuhan.
translations.idiomatic: They made Establishing-Loyalty General Peng Yue Pacifying-West General and Inspector of Liang, stationed at Fuhan.

sentences.zh: 張天錫之西歸也，李儼將賀肫說儼曰：「以明公神武，將士驍悍，奈何束手於人！

translations.literal: When Zhang Tiansxi was returning west, Li Yan's general He Zhun urged Yan: "With your divine martial prowess and your troops' fierce valor, how can you submit helplessly to another!
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Tiansxi was returning west, Li Yan's general He Zhun urged Li Yan: "With your divine martial prowess and your troops' fierce valor, how can you submit helplessly to another!

sentences.zh: 王猛孤軍遠來，士卒疲弊，且以我請救，必不設備，若乘其怠而擊之，可以得志。

translations.literal: Wang Meng's isolated army has come from afar; his soldiers are weary and spent. Moreover, since we summoned him for rescue, he will surely be unprepared. If we strike while he is slack, we can achieve our aim.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng's isolated army has come from afar; his soldiers are weary and spent. Moreover, since we summoned him for rescue, he will surely be unprepared. If we strike while he is slack, we can achieve our aim.

sentences.zh: 」儼曰：「求救於人以免難，難既免而擊之，天下其謂我何！

translations.literal: Yan said: "We begged others for rescue to escape disaster; once the disaster is past, to strike them—what would the world say of us!
translations.idiomatic: Li Yan said: "We begged others for rescue to escape disaster; once the disaster is past, to strike them—what would the world say of us!

sentences.zh: 不若因守以老之，彼將自退」。

translations.literal: Better to hold fast and wear them down; they will withdraw on their own."
translations.idiomatic: Better to hold fast and wear them down; they will withdraw on their own."

sentences.zh: 猛責儼以不即出迎，儼以賀肫之謀告；

translations.literal: Meng rebuked Yan for not coming out at once to welcome him; Yan told him of He Zhun's plot;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng rebuked Li Yan for not coming out at once to welcome him; Li Yan told him of He Zhun's plot;

sentences.zh: 猛斬肫，以儼歸。

translations.literal: Meng beheaded Zhun and took Yan back with him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng beheaded He Zhun and took Li Yan back with him.

sentences.zh: 至長安，堅以儼為光祿勳，賜爵歸安侯。

translations.literal: On reaching Chang'an, Jian made Yan Director of the Imperial Household and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Gui'an.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Chang'an, Fu Jian made Li Yan Director of the Imperial Household and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Gui'an.

sentences.zh: 燕太原桓王恪言於燕主暐曰：「吳王垂，將相之才，十倍於臣。

translations.literal: Murong Ke, Prince of Taiyuan, said to the Yan ruler Wei: "Prince of Wu Murong Chui has the talent of general and chancellor, ten times my own.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ke, Prince of Taiyuan, said to Emperor Murong Wei: "Prince of Wu Murong Chui has the talent of general and chancellor, ten times my own.

sentences.zh: 先帝以長幼之次，故臣得先之。

translations.literal: The late emperor, considering the order of seniority, allowed me to take precedence.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor, considering the order of seniority, allowed me to take precedence.

sentences.zh: 臣死之後，願陛下舉國以聽吳王。

translations.literal: After I die, I hope Your Majesty will entrust the whole realm to Prince of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: After I die, I hope Your Majesty will entrust the whole realm to Prince of Wu.

sentences.zh: 」五月，壬辰，恪疾篤。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on renchen day, Ke's illness grew critical.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on renchen day, Murong Ke's illness grew critical.

sentences.zh: 暐親視之，問以後事。

translations.literal: Wei visited him in person and asked about affairs after his death.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Murong Wei visited him in person and asked about affairs after his death.

sentences.zh: 恪曰：「臣聞報恩莫大於薦賢，賢者雖在板築，猶可為相，況至親乎！

translations.literal: Ke said: "I have heard that no gratitude is greater than recommending the worthy. A worthy man, though he be among wall-builders, may still serve as chancellor—how much more so a close kinsman!
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ke said: "I have heard that no gratitude is greater than recommending the worthy. A worthy man, though he be among wall-builders, may still serve as chancellor—how much more so a close kinsman!

sentences.zh: 吳王文武兼資，管、蕭之亞。

translations.literal: Prince of Wu combines civil and military gifts; he ranks next after Guan Zhong and Xiao He.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Wu Murong Chui combines civil and military gifts; he ranks next after Guan Zhong and Xiao He.

sentences.zh: 陛下若任以大政，國家可安。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty entrusts him with great affairs of state, the realm can be secured.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty entrusts him with great affairs of state, the realm can be secured.

sentences.zh: 不然，秦、晉必有窺窬之計。

translations.literal: Otherwise Qin and Jin will surely harbor designs of opportunistic encroachment.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise Qin and Jin will surely harbor designs of opportunistic encroachment.

sentences.zh: 」言終而卒。

translations.literal: When he had finished speaking, he died.
translations.idiomatic: When he had finished speaking, he died.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅聞恪卒，陰有圖燕之計，欲覘其可否，命匈奴曹轂發使如燕朝貢，以西戎主簿馮翊郭辯為之副。

translations.literal: King of Qin Fu Jian, hearing of Ke's death, secretly formed a plan against Yan and wished to probe whether it was feasible. He ordered the Xiongnu chief Cao Gu to dispatch envoys to Yan with tribute, with Fufeng clerk of the Western Rong Guo Bian as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian of Qin, hearing of Murong Ke's death, secretly formed a plan against Yan and wished to probe whether it was feasible. He ordered the Xiongnu chief Cao Gu to dispatch envoys to Yan with tribute, with Fufeng clerk of the Western Rong Guo Bian as deputy.

sentences.zh: 燕司空皇甫真兄腆及從子奮、覆皆仕秦，腆為散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Yan's Minister of Works Huangfu Zhen's elder brother Tian and his nephews Fen and Fu all served Qin; Tian was a Regular Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's Minister of Works Huangfu Zhen's elder brother Tian and his nephews Fen and Fu all served Qin; Tian was a Regular Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 辯至燕，歷造公卿，謂真曰：「僕本秦人，家為秦所誅，故寄命曹王，貴兄常侍及奮、覆兄弟並相知有素。

translations.literal: When Bian reached Yan, he visited the nobles and high officials in turn and said to Zhen: "I am originally a man of Qin; my family was executed by Qin, so I placed my life in the care of King Cao. Your honored elder brother the Regular Attendant and the brothers Fen and Fu have long known me well.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Bian reached Yan, he visited the nobles and high officials in turn and said to Huangfu Zhen: "I am originally a man of Qin; my family was executed by Qin, so I placed my life in the care of King Cao. Your honored elder brother the Regular Attendant and the brothers Fen and Fu have long known me well.

sentences.zh: 」真怒曰：「臣無境外之交，此言何以及我！

translations.literal: Zhen said angrily: "As a minister I have no dealings beyond the border—how does this concern me!
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Zhen said angrily: "As a minister I have no dealings beyond the border—how does this concern me!

sentences.zh: 君似奸人，得無因緣假托乎！

translations.literal: You seem a treacherous man—is this not some opportunistic pretense!
translations.idiomatic: You seem a treacherous man—is this not some opportunistic pretense!

sentences.zh: 」白暐，請窮治之，太傅評不許。

translations.literal: He reported this to Wei and requested a thorough investigation; Grand Tutor Ping did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: He reported this to Emperor Murong Wei and requested a thorough investigation; Grand Tutor Murong Ping did not permit it.

sentences.zh: 辯還，為堅言：「燕朝政無綱紀，實可圖也。

translations.literal: Bian returned and told Jian: "Yan's court lacks governance and discipline—it can indeed be targeted.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Bian returned and told Fu Jian: "Yan's court lacks governance and discipline—it can indeed be targeted.

sentences.zh: 鑒機識變，唯皇甫真耳。

translations.literal: Only Huangfu Zhen discerns the moment and reads change.
translations.idiomatic: Only Huangfu Zhen discerns the moment and reads change.

sentences.zh: 」堅曰：「以六州之眾，豈得不使有智士一人哉！

translations.literal: Jian said: "With the population of six provinces, can there fail to be even one man of wisdom!
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian said: "With the population of six provinces, can there fail to be even one man of wisdom!

sentences.zh: 曹轂尋卒，秦分其部落為二，使其二子分統之，號東、西曹。

translations.literal: Cao Gu soon died. Qin divided his tribe in two and had his two sons each command one part, styled Eastern and Western Cao.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Gu soon died. Qin divided his tribe in two and had his two sons each command one part, styled Eastern and Western Cao.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史桓豁、竟陵太守羅崇攻宛，拔之。

translations.literal: Inspector of Jing Huan Huo and Grand Administrator of Jingling Luo Chong attacked Wan and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector of Jing Huan Huo and Grand Administrator of Jingling Luo Chong attacked Wan and took it.

sentences.zh: 趙億走，趙盤退歸魯陽。

translations.literal: Zhao Yi fled; Zhao Pan withdrew to Luyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yi fled; Zhao Pan withdrew to Luyang.

sentences.zh: 豁追擊盤於雉城，擒之，留兵戌宛而還。

translations.literal: Huo pursued Pan to Zhicheng, captured him, left troops to garrison Wan, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Huo pursued Pan to Zhicheng, captured him, left troops to garrison Wan, and returned.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，燕下邳王厲等破敕勒，獲馬牛數萬頭。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, King of Xiapi Li of Yan and others defeated the Tiele and seized tens of thousands of horses and cattle.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, King of Xiapi Murong Li of Yan and others defeated the Tiele and seized tens of thousands of horses and cattle.

sentences.zh: 初，厲兵過代地，犯其穄田；

translations.literal: Earlier, when Li's army passed through Dai territory, it violated their millet fields;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Murong Li's army passed through Dai territory, it violated their millet fields;

sentences.zh: 代王什翼犍怒。

translations.literal: The Dai king Shiyijian was enraged.
translations.idiomatic: The Dai king Shiyijian was enraged.

sentences.zh: 燕平北將軍武強公以幽州兵戌雲中。

translations.literal: Yan Pacifying-North General Duke of Wuqiang garrisoned Yunzhong with You Province troops.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Pacifying-North General Duke of Wuqiang garrisoned Yunzhong with You Province troops.

sentences.zh: 八月，什翼犍攻雲中，泥棄城走，振威將軍慕輿賀辛戰沒。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Shiyijian attacked Yunzhong; Ni abandoned the city and fled; Flourishing-Power General Murong Hexin died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Shiyijian attacked Yunzhong; Murong Ni abandoned the city and fled; Flourishing-Power General Murong Hexin died in battle.

sentences.zh: 九月，以會稽內史郗愔為都督徐、兗、青、幽、場州之晉陵諸軍事、徐、兗二州刺史，鎮京口。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Interior Secretary of Kuaiji Xi Yin was made Supervisor of military affairs for Jinling and related matters across Xu, Yan, Qing, You, and Yang provinces, and Inspector of Xu and Yan, stationed at Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Interior Secretary of Kuaiji Xi Yin was made Supervisor of military affairs for Jinling and related matters across Xu, Yan, Qing, You, and Yang provinces, and Inspector of Xu and Yan, stationed at Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 秦淮南公幼之反也，征東大將軍、并州牧、晉公柳、征西大將軍、秦州刺史趙公雙，皆與之通謀。

translations.literal: When Duke of Huainan You of Qin rebelled, East-Campaign Grand General, Governor of Bing Province, Duke of Jin Liu, and West-Campaign Grand General, Inspector of Qin Province, Duke of Zhao Shuang, were all in secret collusion with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke of Huainan Fu You of Qin rebelled, East-Campaign Grand General, Governor of Bing Province, Duke of Jin Fu Liu, and West-Campaign Grand General, Inspector of Qin Province, Duke of Zhao Fu Shuang, were all in secret collusion with him.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅以雙、母弟至親。

translations.literal: King of Qin Fu Jian, because Shuang was his younger brother by the same mother and thus very close kin, concealed the matter and did not investigate.
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian of Qin, because Fu Shuang was his younger brother by the same mother and thus very close kin, concealed the matter and did not investigate.

sentences.zh: 柳，健之愛子，隱而不問。

translations.literal: As for Liu, a beloved younger brother, Fu Jian likewise concealed the matter and did not investigate.
translations.idiomatic: As for Fu Liu, a beloved younger brother, Fu Jian likewise concealed the matter and did not investigate.

sentences.zh: 柳、雙復與鎮東將軍、洛州刺史魏公廋、安西將軍、雍州刺史燕公武謀作亂，鎮東主簿南安姚眺諫曰：「明公以周、郡之親，受方面之任，國家有難，當竭力除之，況自為難乎！

translations.literal: Liu and Shuang again joined East-Pacifying General, Inspector of Luo Province, Duke of Wei Pi, West-Pacifying General, Inspector of Yong Province, Duke of Yan Wu in plotting rebellion. Chief clerk of East-Pacifying, Yao Tiao of Nan'an, remonstrated: "My lord, by kinship close as the Zhou and Shao, you hold a regional command. When the state is in peril one should strive to remove it—how much less create peril oneself!
translations.idiomatic: Fu Liu and Fu Shuang again joined East-Pacifying General, Inspector of Luo Province, Duke of Wei Fu Pi, West-Pacifying General, Inspector of Yong Province, Duke of Yan Fu Wu in plotting rebellion. Chief clerk of East-Pacifying, Yao Tiao of Nan'an, remonstrated: "My lord, by kinship close as the Zhou and Shao, you hold a regional command. When the state is in peril one should strive to remove it—how much less create peril oneself!

sentences.zh: 」廋不聽。

translations.literal: Pi did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi did not listen.

sentences.zh: 堅聞之，徵柳等詣長安。

translations.literal: Jian heard of it and summoned Liu and the others to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian heard of it and summoned Liu and the others to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，柳卯據蒲阪，雙據上邽，廋據陝城，武據安定，皆舉兵反。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Liu seized Puyuan, Shuang seized Shanggui, Pi seized Shancheng, Wu seized Anding—they all raised troops in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, Fu Liu seized Puyuan, Fu Shuang seized Shanggui, Fu Pi seized Shancheng, Fu Wu seized Anding—they all raised troops in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 堅遣使諭之曰：「吾待卿等，恩亦至矣，何苦而反！

translations.literal: Jian sent envoys to instruct them: "I have treated you with the utmost grace—why this bitter rebellion!
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian sent envoys to instruct them: "I have treated you with the utmost grace—why this bitter rebellion!

sentences.zh: 今止不征，卿宜罷兵，各安其位，一切如故。

translations.literal: Now I halt the campaign. You should disband your armies, each resume your post—all shall be as before.
translations.idiomatic: Now I halt the campaign. You should disband your armies, each resume your post—all shall be as before.

sentences.zh: 」各嚙梨以為信。

translations.literal: Each bit a pear as pledge of faith.
translations.idiomatic: Each bit a pear as pledge of faith.

sentences.zh: 皆不從。

translations.literal: None of them complied.
translations.idiomatic: None of them complied.

sentences.zh: 代王什翼犍擊劉衛辰，河冰未合，什翼犍命以葦絲亙約流澌。

translations.literal: The Dai king Shiyijian attacked Liu Weichen. The river ice had not yet closed; Shiyijian ordered reed threads stretched across the floating ice floes.
translations.idiomatic: The Dai king Shiyijian attacked Liu Weichen. The river ice had not yet closed; Shiyijian ordered reed threads stretched across the floating ice floes.

sentences.zh: 俄而冰合，然猶未堅，乃散葦於其上，冰草相結，有如浮梁，代兵乘之以渡。

translations.literal: Soon the ice closed over, but it was still not solid. They then scattered reeds upon it; ice and reeds bound together like a floating bridge, and the Dai troops crossed riding upon it.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the ice closed over, but it was still not solid. They then scattered reeds upon it; ice and reeds bound together like a floating bridge, and the Dai troops crossed riding upon it.

sentences.zh: 衛辰不意兵猝至，與宗族西走，什翼犍收其部落什六七而還。

translations.literal: Weichen did not expect the army to arrive so suddenly; he fled west with his clan. Shiyijian gathered six or seven tenths of his tribes and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Weichen did not expect the army to arrive so suddenly; he fled west with his clan. Shiyijian gathered six or seven tenths of his tribes and returned.

sentences.zh: 衛辰奔秦，秦王堅送衛辰還朔方，遣兵戌之。

translations.literal: Weichen fled to Qin. King of Qin Fu Jian sent Weichen back to Shuofang and dispatched troops to garrison him.
translations.idiomatic: Weichen fled to Qin. King Fu Jian of Qin sent Weichen back to Shuofang and dispatched troops to garrison him.

sentences.zh: 十二月，甲子，燕太尉建寧敬公陽騖卒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on jiazi day, Yang Yu, Grand Commandant and Duke of Jianning, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on jiazi day, Yang Yu, Grand Commandant and Duke of Jianning, died.

sentences.zh: 以司空皇甫真為侍中、太尉，光祿大夫李洪為司空。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Huangfu Zhen was made Palace Attendant and Grand Commandant; Household Director Li Hong was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Huangfu Zhen was made Palace Attendant and Grand Commandant; Household Director Li Hong was made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 孝宗穆皇帝下太和三年（

translations.literal: The third year of Taihe under Emperor Xiaozong Mu (
translations.idiomatic: Third year of Taihe, reign of Emperor Xiaozong Mu (

sentences.zh: 戊辰，公元三六八年）

translations.literal: wuchen, AD 368)
translations.idiomatic: wuchen year, AD 368)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，秦王堅遣後將軍楊成世、左將軍毛嵩分討上邽、安定，輔國將軍王猛、建節將軍鄧羌攻蒲阪、前將軍楊安、廣武將軍張蚝攻陝城。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, King of Qin Fu Jian sent Rear General Yang Chengshi and Left General Mao Song to separately suppress Shanggui and Anding; Aid-the-State General Wang Meng and Standard-Bearer General Deng Qiang attacked Puban; Forward General Yang An and Flourishing-Military General Zhang Hao attacked Shancheng.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, King Fu Jian of Qin sent Rear General Yang Chengshi and Left General Mao Song to suppress Shanggui and Anding respectively, while Aid-the-State General Wang Meng and Standard-Bearer General Deng Qiang attacked Puban and Forward General Yang An and Flourishing-Military General Zhang Hao attacked Shancheng.

sentences.zh: 堅命蒲、陝之軍皆距城三十里，堅壁勿戰，俟秦、雍已平，然後並力取之。

translations.literal: Fu Jian ordered the armies at Puban and Shancheng each to encamp thirty li from the cities, fortify their camps and not give battle, wait until Qin and Yong were pacified, then combine forces to take them.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian ordered the armies at Puban and Shancheng to encamp thirty li from the cities, hold their fortified camps without fighting, wait until Qin and Yong were pacified, and then combine their strength to take the cities.

sentences.zh: 初，燕太宰恪有疾，以燕主暐幼弱，政不在己，太傅評多猜忌，恐大司馬之任不當其人，謂暐兄樂安王臧曰：「今南有遺晉，西有強秦，二國常蓄進取之志，顧我未有隙耳。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yan Grand Preceptor Ke was ill. Because the Yan ruler Wei was young and weak and governance was not in his hands, and Grand Tutor Ping was much given to suspicion and jealousy, he feared the post of Grand Marshal might not go to the right man. He said to Wei's elder brother, Prince of Le'an Zang: "To the south we have the remnant Jin; to the west, powerful Qin. Both states constantly harbor designs of advance—they merely await an opening in us.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yan Grand Preceptor Murong Ke was ill. Because Emperor Murong Wei was still young and weak and power did not rest with Ke himself, and Grand Tutor Murong Ping was much given to suspicion, Ke feared the Grand Marshal's post might not fall to the right man. He said to the emperor's elder brother, Prince of Le'an Murong Zang: "To the south lies the remnant Jin; to the west, powerful Qin. Both states constantly harbor designs of conquest—they are only waiting for us to show a gap.

sentences.zh: 夫國之興衰，系於輔相。

translations.literal: The rise and fall of a state depends on its chancellor and counsellors.
translations.idiomatic: The rise and fall of a state depends on its chancellor and counsellors.

sentences.zh: 大司馬總統六軍，不可任非其人。

translations.literal: The Grand Marshal commands all six armies—one cannot appoint the wrong man.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Marshal commands all six armies; one cannot put the wrong man in that post.

sentences.zh: 我死之後，以親疏言之，當在汝及沖。

translations.literal: After I die, speaking of closeness of kin, the post ought to fall to you and Chong.
translations.idiomatic: After I die, speaking in terms of closeness of kin, the post ought to fall to you and Murong Chong.

sentences.zh: 汝曹雖才識明敏，然年少，未堪多難。

translations.literal: You are clever and perceptive, yet young and not yet equal to many hardships.
translations.idiomatic: You are clever and perceptive, yet still young and not yet equal to many hardships.

sentences.zh: 吳王天資英傑，智略超世，汝曹若能推大司馬以授之，必能混壹四海，況外寇，不足憚也；

translations.literal: The Prince of Wu is gifted by nature, heroic and outstanding, with wisdom and strategy surpassing his age. If you can yield the Grand Marshal's post and entrust it to him, he will surely be able to unify all within the four seas—much less need you fear foreign invaders;
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Wu is gifted by nature, heroic and outstanding, with wisdom and strategy beyond his age. If you can yield the Grand Marshal's post and entrust it to him, he will surely unify the realm under Heaven—much less need you fear foreign invaders;

sentences.zh: 慎無冒利而忘害，不以國家為意也。

translations.literal: Take care not to court profit and forget harm, nor fail to put the state first.
translations.idiomatic: Take care not to chase profit and forget danger, nor fail to put the state first.

sentences.zh: 」又以語太傅評。

translations.literal: " He also spoke thus to Grand Tutor Ping.
translations.idiomatic: " He also spoke thus to Grand Tutor Murong Ping.

sentences.zh: 及恪卒，評不用其言。

translations.literal: When Ke died, Ping did not follow his advice.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Ke died, Murong Ping did not follow his advice.

sentences.zh: 二月，以車騎將軍中山王沖為大司馬。

translations.literal: In the second month, Cavalry General Chong, Prince of Zhongshan, was made Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Cavalry General Murong Chong, Prince of Zhongshan, was made Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 沖，暐之弟也。

translations.literal: Chong was Wei's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chong was Murong Wei's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 以荊州刺史吳王垂為侍中、車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: Inspector of Jing Chui, Prince of Wu, was made Palace Attendant, Grand Cavalry General, and granted honors equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui, Prince of Wu and Inspector of Jing, was made Palace Attendant, Grand Cavalry General, and granted honors equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 秦魏公廋以陝城降燕，請兵應接；

translations.literal: Duke of Wei Pi of Qin surrendered Shancheng to Yan and requested troops for support;
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Wei Fu Pi of Qin surrendered Shancheng to Yan and requested troops to support him;

sentences.zh: 秦人大懼，盛兵守華陰。

translations.literal: The people of Qin were greatly afraid and massed troops to defend Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Qin were greatly afraid and massed troops to defend Huayin.

sentences.zh: 燕魏尹范陽王德上疏，以為：「先帝應天受命，志平六合；

translations.literal: Yan Governor of Wei De, Prince of Fanyang, submitted a memorial, stating: "The late emperor received Heaven's mandate and aspired to pacify the realm;
translations.idiomatic: Murong De, Prince of Fanyang and Governor of Wei in Yan, submitted a memorial, stating: "The late emperor received Heaven's mandate and aspired to pacify the realm;

sentences.zh: 陛下纂統，當繼而成之。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has succeeded to the throne and ought to carry his work to completion.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has succeeded to the throne and ought to carry that work to completion.

sentences.zh: 今苻氏骨肉乖離，國分為五，投誠請援，前後相尋，是天以秦賜燕也。

translations.literal: Now the Fu clan is divided within, the state split into five parts, and men are surrendering in good faith and begging for aid one after another—Heaven is presenting Qin to Yan as a gift.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Fu clan is torn apart within, the state divided into five parts, and men are surrendering in good faith and begging for aid in succession—Heaven is presenting Qin to Yan as a gift.

sentences.zh: 天與不取，反受其殃，吳、越之事，足以觀矣。

translations.literal: Heaven's gift unclaimed brings disaster in turn; the affair of Wu and Yue is lesson enough to read.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's gift refused brings disaster in turn; the affair of Wu and Yue is warning enough.

sentences.zh: 宜命皇甫真引並、冀之眾徑趨蒲阪，吳王垂引許、洛之兵馳解廋圍，太傅總京師虎旅為二年後繼，傳檄三輔，示以禍福，明立購賞，彼必望風響應。

translations.literal: You should order Huangfu Zhen to lead the forces of Bing and Ji straight toward Puban, and Chui, Prince of Wu, to lead the troops of Xu and Luo to speed to relieve Pi's siege; the Grand Tutor should command the capital's elite tiger brigades as rear reserve for the two front armies; issue proclamations throughout the Three Metropolises, showing fortune and disaster and clearly posting rewards—they will surely answer at the wind's first stir.
translations.idiomatic: You should order Huangfu Zhen to lead the forces of Bing and Ji straight toward Puban, and Murong Chui to lead the troops of Xu and Luo to speed to relieve Fu Pi's siege; the Grand Tutor should command the capital's elite tiger brigades as rear reserve for the two front armies; issue proclamations throughout the Three Metropolises, showing fortune and disaster and clearly posting rewards—they will surely rally at the first report.

sentences.zh: 渾一之期，於此乎在矣！

translations.literal: The day of complete unification lies at hand!
translations.idiomatic: The day of complete unification lies at hand!

sentences.zh: 時燕人多請救陝，因圖關中者，太傅評曰：「秦，大國也，今雖有難，未易可圖。

translations.literal: At the time many in Yan urged rescuing Shancheng and seizing the chance to take Guanzhong. Grand Tutor Ping said: "Qin is a great state. Though it is now in difficulty, it is not easily to be targeted.
translations.idiomatic: At the time many in Yan urged rescuing Shancheng and seizing the chance to take Guanzhong. Grand Tutor Murong Ping said: "Qin is a great state. Though it is now in difficulty, it is not easily targeted.

sentences.zh: 朝廷雖明，未如先帝；

translations.literal: Though the court is enlightened, it is not like the late emperor;
translations.idiomatic: Though the court is enlightened, it is not like the late emperor;

sentences.zh: 吾等智略，又非太宰之比。

translations.literal: our wisdom and plans, moreover, do not compare with the Grand Preceptor's.
translations.idiomatic: our wisdom and plans, moreover, do not compare with the Grand Preceptor's.

sentences.zh: 但能閉關保境足矣，平秦非吾事也。

translations.literal: Keeping the gates closed and preserving our borders is enough; pacifying Qin is not our business.
translations.idiomatic: Keeping the gates closed and preserving our borders is enough; pacifying Qin is not our business.

sentences.zh: 魏公廋遺吳王垂及皇甫真箋曰：「苻堅、王猛，皆人傑也，謀為燕患久矣；

translations.literal: Duke of Wei Pi sent letters to Chui, Prince of Wu, and Huangfu Zhen, saying: "Fu Jian and Wang Meng are both outstanding men who have long schemed to bring trouble to Yan;
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Wei Fu Pi sent letters to Murong Chui, Prince of Wu, and Huangfu Zhen, saying: "Fu Jian and Wang Meng are both outstanding men who have long schemed to bring trouble to Yan;

sentences.zh: 今不乘機取之，恐異日燕之君臣將有甬東之悔矣！

translations.literal: If we do not seize this opportunity now, I fear Yan's ruler and ministers will one day rue their plight as Goujian did at Yongdong!
translations.idiomatic: If we do not seize this opportunity now, I fear Yan's ruler and ministers will one day rue their exile to Yongdong as King Goujian did!

sentences.zh: 」垂謂真曰：「方今為人患者必在於秦。

translations.literal: " Chui said to Zhen: "The menace facing us today surely lies in Qin.
translations.idiomatic: " Murong Chui said to Huangfu Zhen: "The menace facing us today surely lies in Qin.

sentences.zh: 主上富於春秋，觀太傅識度，豈能敵苻堅、王猛乎？

translations.literal: The ruler is still young in years; look at the Grand Tutor's vision and capacity—can he match Fu Jian and Wang Meng?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor is still young in years; look at the Grand Tutor's vision and capacity—can he match Fu Jian and Wang Meng?

sentences.zh: 」真曰：「然，吾雖知之，如言不用何！

translations.literal: " Zhen said: "True. I know it myself—but what use if our words are not heeded!
translations.idiomatic: " Huangfu Zhen said: "True. I know it myself—but what use if our words are not heeded!

sentences.zh: 三月，丁巳朔，日月食之。

translations.literal: In the third month, on dingsi day, the first of the month, there was a solar and lunar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on dingsi day, the first of the month, there was a solar and lunar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，大赦。

translations.literal: On guihai day, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai day, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 秦楊成世為趙公雙將苟興所敗，毛嵩亦為燕公武所敗，奔還。

translations.literal: Qin's Yang Chengshi was defeated by Gou Xing, general to Duke of Zhao Shuang; Mao Song was also defeated by Duke of Yan Wu and fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Qin's Yang Chengshi was defeated by Gou Xing, general to Duke of Zhao Fu Shuang; Mao Song was also defeated by Duke of Yan Fu Wu and fled back.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅復遣武衛將軍王鑒、寧朔將軍呂光、將軍馮翊郭將、翟辱等帥眾三萬討之。

translations.literal: King of Qin Fu Jian again sent Guard General Wang Jian, Pacifying-North General Lü Guang, and Generals Guo Jiang of Fufeng and Zhai Ru and others to lead thirty thousand men to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian of Qin again sent Guard General Wang Jian, Pacifying-North General Lü Guang, and Generals Guo Jiang of Fufeng and Zhai Ru and others to lead thirty thousand men to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，雙、武乘勝至於榆眉，以苟興為前鋒。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Shuang and Wu, pressing their victory, reached Yumei, with Gou Xing as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Fu Shuang and Fu Wu, pressing their victory, reached Yumei, with Gou Xing as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 王鑒欲速戰，呂光曰：「興新得志，氣勢方銳，宜持重以待之。

translations.literal: Wang Jian wished to fight quickly. Lü Guang said: "Xing has just tasted success and his spirit is at its keenest—we should hold firm and await him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian wished to fight quickly. Lü Guang said: "Xing has just tasted success and his spirit is at its keenest—we should hold firm and await him.

sentences.zh: 彼糧盡必退，退而擊之，蔑不濟矣！

translations.literal: When their grain is exhausted they will surely retreat; strike them in retreat and nothing will fail!
translations.idiomatic: When their grain runs out they will surely retreat; strike them in retreat and nothing will fail!

sentences.zh: 」二旬而興退。

translations.literal: " After twenty days Xing withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: " After twenty days Xing withdrew.

sentences.zh: 光曰：「興可擊矣。

translations.literal: Lü Guang said: "Xing can be attacked.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang said: "Xing can be attacked now.

sentences.zh: 」遂追之，興敗。

translations.literal: " They pursued him at once; Xing was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: " They pursued him at once and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 因擊雙、武，大破之，斬獲萬五千級。

translations.literal: They then struck Shuang and Wu, routing them thoroughly and taking fifteen thousand heads in kill and capture.
translations.idiomatic: They then struck Fu Shuang and Fu Wu, routing them thoroughly and taking fifteen thousand heads in kill and capture.

sentences.zh: 武棄安定，與雙皆奔上邽，鑒等進攻之。

translations.literal: Wu abandoned Anding and fled with Shuang to Shanggui; Jian and the others pressed the attack.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Wu abandoned Anding and fled with Fu Shuang to Shanggui; Wang Jian and the others pressed the attack.

sentences.zh: 晉公柳數出挑戰，王猛不應。

translations.literal: Duke of Jin Liu repeatedly sallied forth to challenge; Wang Meng did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Jin Fu Liu repeatedly sallied forth to challenge; Wang Meng did not respond.

sentences.zh: 柳以猛為畏之。

translations.literal: Liu took it that Wang Meng feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Liu took it that Wang Meng feared him.

sentences.zh: 五月，留其世子良守蒲阪，帥眾二萬西趨長安。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he left his heir Liang to hold Puban and led twenty thousand men west toward Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he left his heir Fu Liang to hold Puban and led twenty thousand men west toward Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 去蒲阪百餘里，鄧羌帥銳騎七千夜襲，敗之。

translations.literal: When he was a hundred-odd li from Puban, Deng Qiang led seven thousand picked horsemen in a night attack and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: When he was a little over a hundred li from Puban, Deng Qiang led seven thousand picked horsemen in a night attack and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 柳引軍還，猛邀擊之，盡俘其眾。

translations.literal: Liu led his army back; Wang Meng intercepted and struck, capturing his entire force.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Liu led his army back; Wang Meng intercepted and struck, capturing his entire force.

sentences.zh: 柳與數百騎入城，猛、羌進攻之。

translations.literal: Liu entered the city with several hundred horsemen; Wang Meng and Deng Qiang pressed the attack.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Liu entered the city with several hundred horsemen; Wang Meng and Deng Qiang pressed the attack.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，王鑒等拔上邽，斬雙、武，宥其妻子。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Wang Jian and the others took Shanggui, executed Shuang and Wu, and spared their wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Wang Jian and the others took Shanggui, executed Fu Shuang and Fu Wu, and spared their wives and children.

sentences.zh: 以左衛將軍苻雅為秦州刺史。

translations.literal: Left Guard General Fu Ya was made Inspector of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Left Guard General Fu Ya was made Inspector of Qin.

sentences.zh: 八月，以長樂丕為雍州刺史。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Chang Le Pi was made Inspector of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Chang Le Pi was made Inspector of Yong.

sentences.zh: 九月，王猛等拔蒲阪，斬晉公柳及其妻子。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Wang Meng and the others took Puban and executed Duke of Jin Liu and his wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Wang Meng and the others took Puban and executed Duke of Jin Fu Liu and his wife and children.

sentences.zh: 猛屯蒲阪，遣鄧羌與王鑒等會攻陝城。

translations.literal: Wang Meng garrisoned Puban and sent Deng Qiang to join Wang Jian and the others in attacking Shancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng garrisoned Puban and sent Deng Qiang to join Wang Jian and the others in attacking Shancheng.

sentences.zh: 燕王公、貴戚多占民為廕戶，國之戶口少於私家，倉庫空竭，用度不足。

translations.literal: Many Yan princes and nobles had seized commoners as yin-sheltered households; the state's registered households were fewer than those in private estates, the storehouses empty and exhausted, and expenditures insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Many Yan princes and nobles had seized commoners as yin-sheltered households; the state's registered households were fewer than those held in private estates, the storehouses stood empty, and expenditures fell short.

sentences.zh: 尚書左僕射廣信公悅綰曰：「今三方鼎峙，各有吞併之心。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Left of the Masters of Writing Guan, Duke of Guangxin, said: "Today the three powers stand in tripod rivalry, each harboring designs of absorption.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Left of the Masters of Writing Yue Guan, Duke of Guangxin, said: "Today the three powers stand in tripod rivalry, each harboring designs of absorption.

sentences.zh: 而國家政法不立，豪貴恣橫，至使民戶殫盡，委輸無入，吏斷常俸，戰士絕廩，官貸粟帛以自贍給；

translations.literal: Yet our state's laws and governance are not established, the powerful and noble act as they please, until common households are utterly depleted, tax deliveries cease to enter, officials go without regular salaries, warriors without grain rations, and the government must lend grain and cloth for its own support;
translations.idiomatic: Yet our state's laws and governance are not established, the powerful and noble act as they please, until common households are utterly depleted, tax deliveries cease to enter, officials go without regular salaries, warriors without grain rations, and the government must lend grain and cloth merely to sustain itself;

sentences.zh: 既不可聞於鄰敵，且非所以為治，宜一切罷斷諸廕戶，盡還郡縣。

translations.literal: this cannot be shown to neighboring enemies, nor is it the way to govern. All yin-sheltered households should at once be abolished and the people fully returned to their counties and districts.
translations.idiomatic: this cannot be shown to neighboring enemies, nor is it the way to govern. All yin-sheltered households should at once be abolished and the people fully returned to their counties and districts.

sentences.zh: 」燕主暐從之，使綰專治其事，糾擿奸伏，無敢蔽匿，出戶二十餘萬，舉朝怨怒。

translations.literal: " Emperor Wei of Yan agreed and had Guan take sole charge of the matter. He investigated and exposed hidden wrongdoing; none dared conceal it. More than two hundred thousand households were restored, and the whole court seethed with resentment.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Murong Wei agreed and had Yue Guan take sole charge of the matter. He investigated and exposed hidden wrongdoing; none dared conceal it. More than two hundred thousand households were restored, and the whole court seethed with resentment.

sentences.zh: 綰先有疾，自力厘校戶籍，疾遂亟。

translations.literal: Guan had been ill before; straining himself to examine household registers, his illness swiftly worsened.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Guan had been ill before; straining himself to examine household registers, his illness swiftly worsened.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，卒。

translations.literal: In winter, the eleventh month, he died.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the eleventh month, he died.

sentences.zh: 十二月，秦王猛等拔陝城，獲魏公廋，送長安。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Wang Meng of Qin and the others took Shancheng, captured Duke of Wei Pi, and sent him to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Wang Meng of Qin and the others took Shancheng, captured Duke of Wei Fu Pi, and sent him to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅問其所以反，對曰：「臣本無反心，但以弟兄屢謀逆亂，臣懼並死，故謀反耳。

translations.literal: King of Qin Fu Jian asked why he had rebelled. He answered: "Your servant originally had no heart of rebellion, but because my brothers repeatedly plotted treason, I feared dying with them and so plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian of Qin asked why he had rebelled. He answered: "Your servant originally had no heart of rebellion, but because my brothers repeatedly plotted treason, I feared dying with them and so plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 」堅泣曰：「汝素長者，固知非汝心也；

translations.literal: " Fu Jian wept and said: "You have always been a man of virtue—I knew well it was not your heart;
translations.idiomatic: " Fu Jian wept and said: "You have always been a man of virtue—I knew well it was not your heart;

sentences.zh: 且高祖不可以無後。

translations.literal: moreover the High Ancestor cannot be without heirs.
translations.idiomatic: moreover the High Ancestor cannot be without heirs.

sentences.zh: 」乃賜廋死，原其七子，以長子襲魏公，餘子皆封縣公，以嗣越厲王及諸弟之無後者。

translations.literal: " He then granted Pi death by poison, pardoned his seven sons, had the eldest son inherit the dukedom of Wei, enfeoffed the rest as county dukes, and had them succeed Prince of Yue the Stern and the late emperor's brothers who had left no heirs.
translations.idiomatic: " He then granted Fu Pi death by poison, pardoned his seven sons, had the eldest son inherit the dukedom of Wei, enfeoffed the rest as county dukes, and had them succeed Prince of Yue the Stern and the late emperor's brothers who had left no heirs.

sentences.zh: 苟太后曰：「廋與雙俱反，雙獨不得置後，何也？

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Gou said: "Pi and Shuang both rebelled—why does Shuang alone go without heirs?
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Gou said: "Fu Pi and Fu Shuang both rebelled—why does Fu Shuang alone go without heirs?

sentences.zh: 」堅曰：「天下者，高祖之天下，高祖之子不可以無後。

translations.literal: " Fu Jian said: "The realm belongs to the High Ancestor; his sons cannot be without heirs.
translations.idiomatic: " Fu Jian said: "The realm belongs to the High Ancestor; his sons cannot be without heirs.

sentences.zh: 至於仲群，不顧太后，謀危宗廟，天下之法，不可私也。

translations.literal: As for Zhongqun, he ignored the empress dowager and plotted to endanger the ancestral altars—the law of the realm admits no private favor.
translations.idiomatic: As for Zhongqun, he ignored the empress dowager and plotted to endanger the ancestral altars—the law of the realm admits no private favor.

sentences.zh: 」以范陽公抑為征東大將軍、并州刺史，鎮蒲阪；

translations.literal: " Yi, Duke of Fanyang, was made Grand General Who Conquers the East and Inspector of Bing, stationed at Puban;
translations.idiomatic: " Fu Yi, Duke of Fanyang, was made Grand General Who Conquers the East and Inspector of Bing, stationed at Puban;

sentences.zh: 鄧羌為建武將軍、洛州刺史，鎮陝城。

translations.literal: Deng Qiang was made Flourishing-Military General and Inspector of Luo, stationed at Shancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Qiang was made Flourishing-Military General and Inspector of Luo, stationed at Shancheng.

sentences.zh: 擢姚眺為汲郡太守。

translations.literal: Yao Tiao was promoted to Grand Administrator of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Tiao was promoted to Grand Administrator of Ji.

sentences.zh: 加大司馬溫殊禮，位在諸侯王上。

translations.literal: The Grand Marshal was granted exceptional honors, ranking above the feudal princes.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Marshal was granted exceptional honors, ranking above the feudal princes.

sentences.zh: 是歲，以仇池公楊世為秦州刺史，世弟統為武都太守。

translations.literal: That year Duke of Chouchi Yang Shi was made Inspector of Qin, and Shi's younger brother Yang Tong was made Grand Administrator of Wudu.
translations.idiomatic: That year Yang Shi, Duke of Chouchi, was made Inspector of Qin, and Shi's younger brother Yang Tong was made Grand Administrator of Wudu.

sentences.zh: 世亦稱臣於秦，秦以世為南秦州刺史。

translations.literal: Shi also declared himself vassal to Qin; Qin made Shi Inspector of Southern Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shi also declared himself vassal to Qin; Qin made him Inspector of Southern Qin.
